syntaxes.name: activity text
description: The name/text of the activity (e.g. the game name, the custom status text).

syntaxes.name: activity type
description: The type of the activity (playing, streaming, listening, watching, custom status, competing).

syntaxes.name: activity state
description: The state of the activity, or null if the activity has no state set.

syntaxes.name: activity url
description: The URL of the activity (used for streaming activities), or null if it has none.

syntaxes.name: activity emote
description: The emoji of the activity (used for custom statuses), or null if it has none.

syntaxes.name: activity start
description: The date at which the activity started, or null if it has no start timestamp.

syntaxes.name: activity end
description: The date at which the activity ends, or null if it has no end timestamp.

syntaxes.name: activity details
description: The rich-presence details of the activity, or null if the activity is not a rich presence.

syntaxes.name: activity large image
description: The large image URL of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with activity large image of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: activity large text
description: The large image hover text of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with activity large text of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: activity small image
description: The small image URL of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with activity small image of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: activity small text
description: The small image hover text of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with activity small text of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: activity party size
description: The current party size of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has no party.
examples: reply with activity party size of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: activity party max size
description: The maximum party size of the rich-presence activity, or null if it has no party.
examples: reply with activity party max size of {_activity}

syntaxes.name: application description
description: The description of the application.

syntaxes.name: application owner
description: The user who owns the application.

syntaxes.name: privacy policy url
description: The privacy policy URL of the application, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with privacy policy url of {_app}

syntaxes.name: terms of service url
description: The terms of service URL of the application, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with terms of service url of {_app}

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: avatar url
description: The avatar/icon URL of a Discord entity: a user/member's avatar, a guild's icon, a sticker's image, an application's icon... Co-owned across every type that has one, so "avatar url of %x%" works on any of them. Always a string (the image URL).
examples: reply with avatar url of event-user

syntaxes.name: attachment url
description: The URL of the attachment.

syntaxes.name: file name
description: The file name of the attachment.

syntaxes.name: file extension
description: The file extension of the attachment, or null if it has none.

syntaxes.name: attachment duration
description: The duration of the attachment if it is an audio (voice) file, or null otherwise.

syntaxes.name: [an] audio [attachment]
description: Whether the attachment is an audio file (a voice message). If it is, the 'attachment duration' expression can be used on it.

syntaxes.name: [an] image [attachment]
description: Whether the attachment is an image.

syntaxes.name: [a] video [attachment]
description: Whether the attachment is a video.

syntaxes.name: [a] spoiler [attachment]
description: Whether the attachment is marked as a spoiler.

syntaxes.name: download
description: Saves a message attachment to a file on the server, waiting until the download is complete.

A path ending with '/' or '\', or naming an existing folder, is a folder: the file is saved in it under the attachment's file name. Any other path is the file itself. Missing folders are created, and an existing file is overwritten.
A relative path starts from the server's root folder (where the server jar is).
examples: download loop-value to file "plugins/MyScript/last-%file name of loop-value%"

syntaxes.name: logged user
description: The user who triggered this audit log entry, or null if it is unknown.

syntaxes.name: log action type
description: The action type of the audit log entry (e.g. ban, kick, channel create...).
examples: reply with log action type of {_entry}

syntaxes.name: log reason
description: The reason of the audit log entry, or null if none was provided.

syntaxes.name: guild
description: The guild a Discord entity belongs to: a member's, message's, role's, channel's, webhook's, sticker's, emoji's or scheduled event's guild. Co-owned across every such type, so "guild of %x%" works on any of them (null when the entity is not tied to a guild, e.g. a message from DMs).
examples: reply with name of guild of event-message

syntaxes.name: automod message content
description: The message content that triggered the AutoMod execution.
examples: reply with automod message content of event-automod

syntaxes.name: matched content
description: The substring of the message that matched the AutoMod rule, or null if not provided.
examples: reply with matched content of event-automod

syntaxes.name: matched keyword
description: The keyword that matched the AutoMod rule, or null if not provided.
examples: reply with matched keyword of event-automod

syntaxes.name: automod rule id
description: The ID of the AutoMod rule that was triggered.
examples: reply with automod rule id of event-automod

syntaxes.name: automod action type
description: The trigger type of the AutoMod rule that was triggered (keyword, spam, mention spam...).
examples: reply with automod action type of event-automod

syntaxes.name: alert message id
description: The ID of the alert message sent to moderators, or null if no alert was sent.
examples: reply with alert message id of event-automod

syntaxes.name: banned user
description: The user that this ban applies to.

syntaxes.name: ban reason
description: The reason of the ban, or null if none was provided.

syntaxes.name: token
description: The bot's login token. Build-time only.

syntaxes.name: intents
description: The gateway intents, comma-separated by name (or "default intents" / "all"). Build-time only.

syntaxes.name: member cache policy
description: all / default / none / online / owner / voice. Build-time only.
examples: set member cache policy of {_bot} to "all"

syntaxes.name: cache flags
description: The enabled cache flags, comma-separated by name (or "all" / "default" / "none"). Build-time only.
examples: set cache flags of {_bot} to "activity, voice_state"

syntaxes.name: compression
description: zlib / none. Build-time only.

syntaxes.name: shard count
description: The number of shards. -1 (default) = Discord's recommended count, 1 = single shard, N>=2 = N shards. Build-time only; once running, returns the real shard total.

syntaxes.name: activity
description: The bot's activity. A text is a "playing" activity; use the activity expressions (watching, listening, ...) for the other kinds. Live-updatable.
examples: set activity of {_bot} to watching "the server"

syntaxes.name: gateway ping
description: Average gateway ping across shards, in ms (-1 if not running).

syntaxes.name: guild count
description: Number of guilds the bot is in (0 if not running).

syntaxes.name: running shards
description: Number of currently-connected shards (0 if not running).
examples: send "%running shards of event-bot% shards up"

syntaxes.name: guilds
description: All guilds the bot is a member of (empty if not running).
examples: set {_g} to first element of guilds of event-bot

syntaxes.name: self user
description: The bot's own user account (none if not running).
examples: send "%name of self user of event-bot%"

syntaxes.name: application info
description: The application (developer portal) info of the bot. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_info} to application info of event-bot

syntaxes.name: connected
description: Whether the bot is logged in and running (its shards have been built).

syntaxes.name: connect bot
description: Connects a bot to an audio (voice or stage) channel.
The bot needs the Connect permission on that channel.
examples: connect bot "MyBot" to voice channel with id "000000000000000000"

syntaxes.name: disconnect bot
description: Closes a bot's audio connection in a guild.
Without a bot, the one owning the given guild is used.

syntaxes.name: make bot leave
description: Makes a bot leave a guild. It loses every access to that server until re-invited.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: online status
description: The online status of a Discord entity. Read-only on a member (the presence Discord reports: online, idle, do not disturb, offline...). On a bot it is the live presence and can be set (online / idle / dnd / invisible). One syntax, dispatched per type — "online status of %member/bot%".
examples: reply with online status of event-member

syntaxes.name: avatar url
description: The avatar/icon URL of a Discord entity: a user/member's avatar, a guild's icon, a sticker's image, an application's icon... Co-owned across every type that has one, so "avatar url of %x%" works on any of them. Always a string (the image URL).
examples: reply with avatar url of event-user

entities.name: Discord Command
entities.description: A command declared with the 'discord command' structure. Available as 'event-discordcommand' in its trigger and in the 'discord command used' / 'failed' events, or through 'all discord commands'.

syntaxes.name: description
description: The 'description' entry of the command, if any.
examples: send description of event-discordcommand to console

syntaxes.name: usage
description: The 'usage' entry of the command, or a generated one from its name and arguments.

syntaxes.name: category
description: The 'category' entry of the command, if any.

syntaxes.name: aliases
description: The aliases of the command, without its main name.
examples: send aliases of event-discordcommand to console

syntaxes.name: prefixes
description: The prefixes of the command. Empty when it answers to its bare name.
examples: send prefixes of event-discordcommand to console

syntaxes.name: cooldown
description: The 'cooldown' entry of the command, if any.
examples: send cooldown of event-discordcommand to console

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: error code
description: The Discord error code (e.g. 10008 = Unknown Message), or -1 for a non-Discord error.

syntaxes.name: error meaning
description: The human-readable meaning of the error (JDA's, e.g. "Missing Permissions").

syntaxes.name: error message
description: The full error message.

syntaxes.name: inline
description: Whether the embed field is displayed inline.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: value
description: The value of an embed field. Co-owned with Skript's native Property.TYPED_VALUE, the same property that reads the value of a sign line.

syntaxes.name: description
description: The description (main text) of the embed.

syntaxes.name: title url
description: The URL the embed title links to. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: discord author
description: The author name of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: author icon
description: The author icon URL of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: author url
description: The author URL of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: footer
description: The footer text of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).
examples: set footer of {_embed} to "Powered by DiSky"

syntaxes.name: footer icon
description: The footer icon URL of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: image
description: The image URL of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: thumbnail
description: The thumbnail URL of the embed. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: timestamp
description: The timestamp shown in the embed's footer. Read back is not supported by JDA (returns null).

syntaxes.name: fields
description: The fields of the embed. Add fields with 'add %field% to fields of %embed%'.
examples: add (a new field named "Ping" with value "42ms") to fields of {_embed}

syntaxes.name: title
description: The title of an embed. Co-owned with Skript's native Property.TITLE.

syntaxes.name: color
description: The color of a Discord entity: a role's color, an embed's side bar, or the color a role builder will be created with. On a Skript that has the native Property.COLOR, "color of %x%" is the same expression that colors a block or a firework, dispatched per runtime type; on one that does not, it is "discord color of %x%".
Write-only on a role builder and on an embed builder: JDA exposes no getter on either, so reading them gives <none>.
examples: set color of event-role to orange

entities.name: Emoji
entities.description: Any Discord emoji: a unicode emoji or a custom one (an 'emote'). It displays as the emoji itself, or as <:name:id> for a custom emoji, so it renders when sent.

syntaxes.name: emote image url
description: The URL of the custom emoji's image.
examples: reply with emote image url of {_emote}

syntaxes.name: allowed roles
description: The roles allowed to use a guild emote. Empty means everyone can use it.
examples: send "%size of allowed roles of {_emote}% role(s) can use it" to console

syntaxes.name: animated
description: Whether the custom emoji is animated.

syntaxes.name: suppress reactions
description: Removes one or more reactions from a message.
Naming a user removes that user's reaction; without one, the bot's own reaction is removed.
examples: suppress reaction emoji "x" of event-user from event-message

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: File Upload
entities.description: A file to send to Discord, created from a local file, a URL or a received attachment. Attach it to a message builder with 'add {_file} to attachments of {_message}'.

syntaxes.name: file name
description: The name the file will carry on Discord, extension included. Can be changed.

syntaxes.name: spoiler
description: Whether Discord hides the file behind a spoiler. It works by prefixing the file name with 'SPOILER_', so rename the file before, not after.

syntaxes.name: file description
description: The alt text of the file, shown by screen readers and on hover for images.
examples: set file description of {_file} to "the server logo"

syntaxes.name: tag emote
description: The emoji of a forum tag, or null if the tag has no emoji.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: description
description: The description of a guild sticker, empty when it has none.

syntaxes.name: sticker tags
description: The tags of a guild sticker: the words or emojis Discord suggests it for.

syntaxes.name: guild
description: The guild a Discord entity belongs to: a member's, message's, role's, channel's, webhook's, sticker's, emoji's or scheduled event's guild. Co-owned across every such type, so "guild of %x%" works on any of them (null when the entity is not tied to a guild, e.g. a message from DMs).
examples: reply with name of guild of event-message

syntaxes.name: members
description: The members of the guild. Without 'await' this is the cached member list, which may be incomplete depending on the bot's cache settings.
With 'await' the full member list is loaded online (this can be slow on large guilds).
examples: await set {_all::*} to members of event-guild

syntaxes.name: afk channel
description: The AFK voice channel of the guild, or null if none is set.
examples: set afk channel of event-guild to voice channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: afk timeout
description: The AFK timeout of the guild, in seconds (60, 300, 900, 1800 or 3600).
examples: set afk timeout of event-guild to 300

syntaxes.name: banner
description: The URL of the guild's banner image, or null if none is set.

syntaxes.name: boost count
description: How many members are currently boosting the guild.
examples: reply with "%boost count of event-guild% booster(s)!"

syntaxes.name: boost role
description: The booster role of the guild (granted to members who boost it), or null if none.
examples: reply with "Thanks %mention tag of boost role of event-guild%!"

syntaxes.name: boost tier
description: The boost tier of the guild (e.g. 'none', 'tier 1', 'tier 2', 'tier 3').
examples: reply with boost tier of event-guild

syntaxes.name: bot role
description: The integration role of this bot in the guild, or null if it has none.
examples: reply with mention tag of bot role of event-guild

syntaxes.name: everyone role
description: The @everyone (public) role of the guild.
examples: reply with mention tag of everyone role of event-guild

syntaxes.name: member count
description: The total number of members in the guild.
examples: reply with "%member count of event-guild% members"

syntaxes.name: verification level
description: The verification level of the guild ('none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'very high').
examples: reply with verification level of event-guild
set verification level of event-guild to "high"

syntaxes.name: boosters
description: The members currently boosting the guild.

syntaxes.name: scheduled events
description: All scheduled events of the guild.
examples: set {_events::*} to scheduled events of event-guild

syntaxes.name: text channels
description: All text channels of the guild.
examples: set {_channels::*} to text channels of event-guild

syntaxes.name: voice channels
description: All voice channels of the guild.
examples: set {_channels::*} to voice channels of event-guild

syntaxes.name: news channels
description: All news (announcement) channels of the guild.
examples: set {_channels::*} to news channels of event-guild

syntaxes.name: stage channels
description: All stage channels of the guild.
examples: set {_channels::*} to stage channels of event-guild

syntaxes.name: categories
description: All channel categories of the guild.

syntaxes.name: guild channels
description: Every guild channel, including text, voice, stage, news and category channels.
examples: set {_channels::*} to guild channels of event-guild

syntaxes.name: roles
description: All roles of the guild, ordered by position (highest first).

syntaxes.name: emojis
description: All custom emojis of the guild.

syntaxes.name: stickers
description: All custom stickers of the guild.

syntaxes.name: invites
description: All active invites of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_invites::*} to invites of event-guild

syntaxes.name: webhooks
description: All webhooks of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_webhooks::*} to webhooks of event-guild

syntaxes.name: welcome screen
description: The welcome screen of the guild, fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Fails when the guild is not a community guild.
examples: await set {_screen} to the welcome screen of event-guild

syntaxes.name: automod rules
description: All AutoMod rules of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_rules::*} to automod rules of event-guild

syntaxes.name: emotes
description: All custom emotes (emojis) of the guild, fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Unlike 'emojis of %guild%' this never depends on the bot's cache.
examples: await set {_emotes::*} to emotes of event-guild

syntaxes.name: bans
description: All bans of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Only the first page (up to 1000 bans) is returned.
examples: await set {_bans::*} to bans of event-guild

syntaxes.name: active threads
description: Every non-archived thread channel of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_threads::*} to active threads of event-guild

syntaxes.name: audit logs
description: The audit log entries of the guild. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Only the most recent page (up to 100 entries) is returned.
examples: await set {_logs::*} to audit logs of event-guild

syntaxes.name: discord owner
description: The owner of the guild, as a member.
Without 'await' this is the cached member, which may be null if the owner is not cached; with 'await' it is fetched online.
examples: reply with discord owner of event-guild
await set {_owner} to discord owner of event-guild

syntaxes.name: guild with id
description: The guild with the given id, looked up in cache.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: avatar url
description: The avatar/icon URL of a Discord entity: a user/member's avatar, a guild's icon, a sticker's image, an application's icon... Co-owned across every type that has one, so "avatar url of %x%" works on any of them. Always a string (the image URL).
examples: reply with avatar url of event-user

syntaxes.name: invite code
description: The code of the invite (the part after discord.gg/).
examples: reply with invite code of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite url
description: The full URL of the invite.
examples: reply with invite url of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite inviter
description: The user who created the invite, or null if it is unknown.
examples: reply with invite inviter of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite max age
description: The maximum age (in seconds) this invite can be used for.
examples: reply with invite max age of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite max uses
description: The maximum amount of times this invite can be used.
examples: reply with invite max uses of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite uses
description: The amount of times this invite has already been used.
examples: reply with invite uses of event-invite

syntaxes.name: invite creation date
description: The date at which the invite was created.
examples: reply with invite creation date of event-invite

syntaxes.name: roles
description: The roles of the member. Add or remove roles to grant/revoke them.
examples: await remove {_role} from roles of event-member

syntaxes.name: join date
description: The date at which the member joined the guild.
examples: reply with join date of event-member

syntaxes.name: boost date
description: The date at which the member started boosting the guild, or null if the member is not boosting.
examples: reply with boost date of event-member

syntaxes.name: flags
description: The flags of the member (e.g. did rejoin, completed onboarding, bypasses verification...). Add or remove modifiable flags to toggle them.
examples: add did rejoin to flags of event-member

syntaxes.name: discord colors
description: The role colors of a member's name in the guild.
Determined by the colors of the highest role assigned to the member that does not have the default colors.
examples: reply with tertiary role color of (colors of event-member)

syntaxes.name: activities
description: All activities of a member (playing, streaming, listening, watching, custom status, competing).
Returns an empty list if the member has no activity.
Requires CacheFlag.ACTIVITY to be enabled on the bot, along with the GUILD_PRESENCES intent.

syntaxes.name: voice channel
description: The audio (voice) channel the member is currently connected to, or null if they are not in a voice channel.
examples: reply with voice channel of event-member

syntaxes.name: discord permissions
description: The effective guild-wide permissions of the member: every permission given by its roles and by @everyone, or all of them for the owner and for an administrator. Channel overrides are not included; use the discord permissions of the member in a channel for that.
Read-only: a member gets its permissions from its roles, so change the roles or the role permissions instead.
examples: set {_perms::*} to discord permissions of event-member
if discord permissions of event-member contain manage messages:

syntaxes.name: muted
description: Whether the member is muted (self or by the guild) in a voice channel.

syntaxes.name: deafened
description: Whether the member is deafened (self or by the guild) in a voice channel.

syntaxes.name: timed out
description: Whether the member is currently timed out in the guild.

syntaxes.name: [a] discord bot
description: Whether the member's account is a Discord bot.
examples: if event-member is a discord bot:

syntaxes.name: has role
description: Whether the member has the given role.

syntaxes.name: can interact
description: Whether the member can interact with (act upon) any of the given members or roles.

syntaxes.name: has permission
description: Whether the member has all the given permissions, either guild-wide or in a specific channel (channel overrides included). An administrator has every permission.
examples: if event-member has discord permission administrator:
if event-member has discord permissions send messages and embed links in event-channel:

syntaxes.name: is in thread
description: Whether the member has joined the given thread. Useful to avoid errors when adding a member to a thread they are already in.
examples: if event-member is in the thread {_thread}:

syntaxes.name: member with id
description: The member with the given id; cache, or online with await.
examples: await set {_m} to member with id "123" in event-guild

syntaxes.name: ban
description: Bans a member from their guild, optionally deleting their recent messages.
The bot needs the Ban Members permission and a role above the target's.
examples: ban event-member because of "spam" and delete 7 days worth of messages

syntaxes.name: deafen
description: Server-deafens a member. The member must be connected to a voice channel.

syntaxes.name: disconnect from voice
description: Disconnects a member from the voice channel they are in.

syntaxes.name: kick
description: Kicks a member from their guild.

syntaxes.name: move to voice channel
description: Moves a member to another voice channel. The member must already be connected.
examples: move event-member to voice channel with id "000000000000000000"

syntaxes.name: mute
description: Server-mutes a member. The member must be connected to a voice channel.

syntaxes.name: remove time out
description: Lifts a member's time out.
examples: remove the time out of event-member

syntaxes.name: time out for
description: Times a member out for a duration (Discord caps it at 28 days).
A timed-out member cannot talk, react, or join voice channels.
examples: time out event-member for 10 minutes due to "flooding"

syntaxes.name: time out until
description: Times a member out until a given date (Discord caps it at 28 days out).
examples: time out event-member until now + 1 hour

syntaxes.name: undeafen
description: Lifts a member's server deafen.

syntaxes.name: unmute
description: Lifts a member's server mute.

syntaxes.name: nickname
description: A guild member's nickname, which is their display name on that guild. Co-owned with Skript's native Property.DISPLAY_NAME, so "nickname of", "display name of" and "custom name of" all reach it.
For the name that falls back to the account name when no nickname is set, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: online status

syntaxes.name: mention tag

syntaxes.name: poll question

syntaxes.name: multi answer

syntaxes.name: poll layout

syntaxes.name: expired
description: Whether the poll has passed its deadline and no longer accepts votes.

syntaxes.name: finalized
description: Whether the poll votes are finalized, meaning the reported vote counts are the definitive ones.

syntaxes.name: discord content
description: Get the raw (non formatted) content of a sent message.

syntaxes.name: discord author
description: Get the user instance of the message's author. Can be null in case of the message was sent by a webhook.

syntaxes.name: member author
description: Get the member instance of the message's author. Can be null if it's in PM or not in guild!

syntaxes.name: referenced message
description: Get the message referenced (replied to) by a specific message, if any.
examples: set {_replied} to referenced message of event-message

syntaxes.name: poll
description: Get the poll attached to a specific message, if any.

syntaxes.name: embeds
description: Get every embed of a specific message, in display order (10 at most).

syntaxes.name: discord attachments

syntaxes.name: reactions
description: Get every reaction of a message.

syntaxes.name: mentioned users
description: Get every mentioned user in a message.

syntaxes.name: mentioned members
description: Get every mentioned member in a message. If the message doesn't come from a guild it will return an empty list!

syntaxes.name: mentioned roles

syntaxes.name: channel

syntaxes.name: mentioned channels
description: Get every mentioned text channel in a message.

syntaxes.name: mentioned voice channels
description: Get every mentioned voice channel in a message.

syntaxes.name: mentioned emotes
description: Get every mentioned emote in a message.

syntaxes.name: discord components
description: Every component of a sent message, rows and containers flattened: the buttons, dropdowns, text displays and so on it carries.

syntaxes.name: using components v2
description: Whether the message is a components V2 message (containers, sections, text displays...).

syntaxes.name: edited
description: Whether the message has been edited.

syntaxes.name: pinned
description: Whether the message is pinned in its channel.

syntaxes.name: ephemeral
description: Whether the message is ephemeral (only visible to one user).

syntaxes.name: tts
description: Whether the message was sent using text-to-speech.

syntaxes.name: from [a] guild
description: Whether the message was sent in a guild channel (rather than a private/DM channel).
examples: if event-message is from a guild:

syntaxes.name: from [a] (dm|private message|direct message)
description: Whether the message was sent in a private (direct message) channel rather than in a guild.
examples: if event-message is from a dm:

syntaxes.name: [a] voice message
description: Whether the message is a voice message. If it is, the 'attachment duration' expression can be used on its attachment.
examples: if event-message is a voice message:

syntaxes.name: forwarded
description: Whether the message is a forwarded message, that is, a message originally sent in another channel and forwarded to this one.

syntaxes.name: [a] poll
description: Whether the message has a poll attached to it.

syntaxes.name: message with id
description: The message with the given id in a channel (requires await).
examples: await set {_msg} to message with id "123" in event-channel

syntaxes.name: edit
description: Replaces a message's content or embeds. Only the bot's own messages can be edited.

syntaxes.name: end poll
description: Ends the poll attached to a message immediately, preventing any further vote.
examples: end the poll of event-message now

syntaxes.name: forward
description: Forwards a message to another channel, creating a copy carrying the 'forwarded' marker.

syntaxes.name: pin
description: Pins a message in its channel. A channel holds up to 50 pinned messages.

syntaxes.name: publish
description: Publishes (crossposts) a message to every guild following its channel.
Only works in a news/announcement channel.

syntaxes.name: purge
description: Deletes several messages at once, using Discord's bulk-delete endpoint.

syntaxes.name: react
description: Adds one or more reactions to a message, as the bot.

syntaxes.name: suppress embeds
description: Hides the link embeds Discord generated for a message.

syntaxes.name: unpin
description: Removes a message from its channel's pins.

syntaxes.name: jump url

syntaxes.name: guild
description: The guild a Discord entity belongs to: a member's, message's, role's, channel's, webhook's, sticker's, emoji's or scheduled event's guild. Co-owned across every such type, so "guild of %x%" works on any of them (null when the entity is not tied to a guild, e.g. a message from DMs).

syntaxes.name: answer votes

syntaxes.name: answer emote
description: The emoji of a poll answer, or null if it has none.

syntaxes.name: answer id

syntaxes.name: answer self voted

syntaxes.name: profile banner

syntaxes.name: profile color

examples: await set {_color} to profile color of (profile of event-user)

syntaxes.name: [a] [custom] banner
description: Whether the profile has a custom banner set. If it does not, the 'profile color' expression returns the accent color instead.
examples: if (profile of event-user) has a custom banner:

syntaxes.name: primary color

syntaxes.name: secondary color

examples: reply with secondary color of (colors of event-role)

syntaxes.name: tertiary color

examples: reply with tertiary color of (colors of event-role)

syntaxes.name: role position
description: The position (ordering index) of the role within the guild's role list.

syntaxes.name: role colors
description: The full color set (primary / secondary / tertiary) of the role (JDA 6.x role colors).
examples: reply with primary color of (role colors of event-role)

syntaxes.name: discord permissions
description: The guild-wide permissions of the role, the ones set in the role settings of the guild (channel overrides are not included; see the allowed and denied discord permissions in a channel).
Set, add and remove change the role on Discord. Setting it to nothing (or deleting it) leaves the role with no permission at all; reset is not supported, since a role has no default to go back to.
The bot needs the 'manage roles' permission, a role below its own highest role, and every permission it gives: Discord refuses to grant a permission the bot does not have itself.
examples: set {_perms::*} to discord permissions of event-role

syntaxes.name: mentionable

syntaxes.name: move role down

syntaxes.name: move role under
description: Moves a role directly below another one of the same guild. Indexes update automatically.
examples: move role {_role} under role with id "000000000000000000"

syntaxes.name: move role up
description: Moves a role up by a number of positions (one by default).

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. syntaxes.name: color

On a Skript that has the native Property.COLOR, "color of %x%" is the same expression that colors a block or a firework, dispatched per runtime type; on one that does not, it is "discord color of %x%".

syntaxes.name: discord location
description: The location of a scheduled event: a channel id for channel-bound events, or the external place.

syntaxes.name: start date
description: The start date of a scheduled event.

syntaxes.name: end date
description: The end date of a scheduled event, or null for channel-bound events.
Settable for external events.
examples: set end date of {_event} to now

syntaxes.name: cover
description: The cover image URL of a scheduled event, or null if no cover is set.
Settable to a URL or local file path.

syntaxes.name: event channel
description: The guild channel a scheduled event is bound to, or null for external events.

syntaxes.name: creator
description: The user who created a scheduled event, or null if unknown.

syntaxes.name: interested members

syntaxes.name: discriminator

syntaxes.name: badges

This does not and cannot contain any intro-related badges (nitro membership or nitro boosting); it needs OAuth2 to be enabled.
examples: reply with "Whoa! You got all of them? %join badges of event-user with nl%"

syntaxes.name: mutual guilds
description: Every guild that the bot and the user have in common.
examples: reply with "Oh boi, we have %size of mutual guilds of event-user% mutual guilds!"

syntaxes.name: profile
description: The profile of a user, which mainly holds the banner and accent color.

syntaxes.name: private channel

examples: await set {_channel} to private channel of event-user

syntaxes.name: primary guild tag

syntaxes.name: primary guild tag icon
description: The icon URL of a user's primary-guild server tag, or null if there is none.
examples: reply with primary guild tag icon of event-user

entities.name: Webhook Client
entities.description: Something that can post messages through a webhook: either a webhook retrieved from a guild or channel, or a client built from a webhook URL alone. A client built from a URL needs no permission in the guild and can post even where no bot is present; it can only send, edit and delete its own messages.

syntaxes.name: webhook token
description: The secret token of the webhook, or nothing when Discord did not expose it (for example a channel follower webhook). Anyone holding it can post through the webhook.

syntaxes.name: webhook post
description: Makes a webhook, or a webhook client built from a URL, post a message.
The username and avatar override the webhook's own for this message only. The sent message is discarded; build a webhook message and read 'the build result of' it to keep it.
examples: make webhook client {_hook} post "Hello from the webhook!"
make {_hook} post {_embed} with username "Announcer" and avatar "https://example.com/a.png"
make {_hook} speak "In a thread" in thread {_thread}

syntaxes.name: new webhook client
description: Creates a webhook client from a webhook URL (including its token).
A bot is only used to carry the HTTP requests; when none is given, the only loaded bot is used.
examples: set {_hook} to a new webhook client from url "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123/abc"
set {_hook} to a new webhook client with url {url} using bot "MyBot"

syntaxes.name: webhook url
description: The URL of the webhook (including its token).

syntaxes.name: webhook channel
description: The channel the webhook posts to.
Set it to a text channel to move the webhook.
examples: set webhook channel of {_webhook} to event-channel

syntaxes.name: webhook owner
description: The member who owns/created the webhook, or null if it is unknown.

syntaxes.name: webhook type
description: The kind of the webhook: INCOMING (posts through its URL) or CHANNEL_FOLLOWER (created by following an announcement channel).

syntaxes.name: webhook avatar
description: The avatar URL of the webhook.
Set it to an image URL or a local file path.

syntaxes.name: webhook source guild id
description: For a channel follower webhook, the id of the guild whose announcements it relays; nothing otherwise.
examples: reply with webhook source guild id of {_webhook}

syntaxes.name: webhook source channel id
description: For a channel follower webhook, the id of the announcement channel it relays; nothing otherwise.
examples: reply with webhook source channel id of {_webhook}

description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: AutoMod Response
entities.description: An action an automod rule takes when it triggers: block the message, send an alert, time the member out or block the member's interactions. Responses are immutable values; build one with the 'new automod response' expressions.

syntaxes.name: response type
description: The kind of action of the response.
examples: if response type of {_r} is timeout:

syntaxes.name: response channel
description: The channel the alert is sent to, or nothing if the response is not an alert.

syntaxes.name: response message
description: The custom message shown when a message is blocked, or nothing if there is none.

syntaxes.name: response timeout
description: The timeout duration of the response, or nothing if the response is not a timeout.

syntaxes.name: new block interaction
patterns: [a] new automod response blocking [the] member interaction[s]
description: Blocks the member from interacting with the server (member profile rules only).
examples: set {_r} to a new automod response blocking the member interactions

syntaxes.name: new block message
patterns: [a] new automod response blocking [the] message [with [the] [custom] message %-string%]
description: Blocks the offending message. The optional custom message (150 characters max) is shown to the member whose message was blocked.
examples: set {_r} to a new automod response blocking the message with the custom message "No spam here"

syntaxes.name: new send alert
patterns: [a] new automod response sending [an] alert to [the] [channel] %standardguildmessagechannel%
description: Sends an alert message to the given channel when the rule triggers.
examples: set {_r} to a new automod response sending an alert to the channel event-channel

syntaxes.name: new timeout
patterns: [a] new automod response timing [the] member out for %timespan%
description: Times the member out for the given duration (keyword and mention spam rules only).
examples: set {_r} to a new automod response timing the member out for 10 minutes

entities.name: AutoMod Rule Builder
entities.description: An automod rule that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then. A rule needs at least one response.

syntaxes.name: new message builder
patterns: [a] new automod rule builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% in [the] [guild] %guild% (for|checking) messages (with|using) [the] [trigger] %triggerconfig%
description: Creates a builder for a rule checked when a message is sent.
examples: set {_t} to a new automod keyword trigger with the keywords "badword"
set {_b} to a new automod rule builder named "No bad words" in event-guild for messages using {_t}
add a new automod response blocking the message to automod responses of {_b}
await set {_rule} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new profile builder
patterns: [a] new automod rule builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% in [the] [guild] %guild% (for|checking) member profiles (with|using) [the] [trigger] %triggerconfig%
description: Creates a builder for a rule checked when a member updates their profile (username, nickname, bio).
Only keyword triggers are accepted, and the block-member-interaction response is added for you.
examples: set {_b} to a new automod rule builder named "Profiles" in event-guild for member profiles using {_t}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the rule on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two rules (Discord limits some trigger types to one per guild).
examples: await set {_rule} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: AutoMod Rule

syntaxes.name: creator
description: The member who created the rule, or nothing if they left the guild or are not cached.

syntaxes.name: creator id
description: The id of the user who created the rule.

syntaxes.name: enabled
description: Whether the rule is currently enforced.

syntaxes.name: automod event type
description: When the rule is checked: on a sent message or on a member profile update.
examples: reply with automod event type of {_rule}

syntaxes.name: automod trigger type
description: What the rule looks for (keyword, spam, keyword preset, mention spam, member profile keyword).
examples: reply with automod trigger type of {_rule}

syntaxes.name: exempt roles
description: The roles whose members are ignored by the rule (20 max).
examples: add role with id "123" to exempt roles of {_rule}

syntaxes.name: exempt channels
description: The channels where the rule does not apply (50 max).

syntaxes.name: automod responses

syntaxes.name: filtered keywords

syntaxes.name: filtered patterns

syntaxes.name: allow list
description: The words that never trigger a keyword or preset rule.

syntaxes.name: presets

syntaxes.name: mention limit

syntaxes.name: mention raid protection

syntaxes.name: trigger config
description: Replaces what the rule looks for. The trigger must be of the same type as the rule's current one.

examples: set trigger config of {_rule} to a new automod keyword trigger with the keywords "spam"

description: The keyword presets of a preset trigger.

syntaxes.name: mention limit
description: The number of mentions above which a mention spam trigger fires (1 to 50).

syntaxes.name: mention raid protection
description: Whether a mention spam trigger also detects mention raids (many members mentioned in a short time).
examples: set mention raid protection of {_t} to true

syntaxes.name: new keyword trigger
description: Matches messages containing one of the keywords. Keywords accept the wildcards '*' at the start, the end or both ("*bad*").
A keyword trigger needs at least one keyword or one pattern when the rule is built.
examples: set {_t} to a new automod keyword trigger with the keywords "badword", "*spoiler*"

syntaxes.name: new mention spam trigger
patterns: [a] new automod mention spam trigger with [a] [mention] limit [of] %number%
description: Matches messages mentioning more unique users and roles than the limit (50 max). Only one rule of this kind per guild.
examples: set {_t} to a new automod mention spam trigger with a limit of 5

syntaxes.name: new pattern trigger
patterns: [a] new automod pattern trigger with [the] [regex] patterns %strings%
description: Matches messages against regex patterns (Rust flavored, 10 patterns of 260 characters max).
examples: set {_t} to a new automod pattern trigger with the patterns "discord[.]gg/.+"

syntaxes.name: new preset trigger
description: Matches messages against Discord's maintained keyword lists. Only one rule of this kind per guild.
examples: set {_t} to a new automod preset trigger with the presets profanity and slurs

syntaxes.name: new spam trigger
description: Matches messages Discord considers spam. Only one rule of this kind per guild.
examples: set {_t} to a new automod spam trigger

entities.name: Channel Builder
entities.description: A channel that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: topic
description: The topic of the channel being built. Text, news, forum and media channels only.
examples: set topic of {_b} to "Rules and announcements"

syntaxes.name: nsfw
description: Whether the channel being built is marked as age-restricted.

syntaxes.name: slowmode
description: The slowmode of the channel being built, in seconds (0 disables it).

syntaxes.name: bitrate
description: The audio bitrate (in bits per second) of the voice/stage channel being built.

syntaxes.name: user limit
description: How many members may join the voice channel being built at once (0 = no limit).

syntaxes.name: region
description: The raw voice region key of the audio channel being built, or none for automatic.

syntaxes.name: channel position
description: The position of the channel being built in its guild's channel list.

syntaxes.name: category
description: The category the channel being built will be placed under.
examples: set category of {_b} to category with id "000"

syntaxes.name: new category builder
description: Creates a category builder. Other channel builders can then be parented to the built category.
examples: set {_b} to a new category builder named "Staff" in event-guild
await set {_category} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new forum channel builder
description: Creates a forum channel builder.
examples: set {_b} to a new forum channel builder named "help" in event-guild
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new media channel builder
description: Creates a media channel builder.
examples: set {_b} to a new media channel builder named "gallery" in event-guild
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new news channel builder
description: Creates an announcement (news) channel builder.
examples: set {_b} to a new news channel builder named "updates" in event-guild
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new stage channel builder
description: Creates a stage channel builder.
examples: set {_b} to a new stage channel builder named "Conference" in event-guild
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new text channel builder
description: Creates a text channel builder. The channel only exists once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new text channel builder named "general" in event-guild
set topic of {_b} to "Talk about anything here"
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new voice channel builder
description: Creates a voice channel builder.
examples: set {_b} to a new voice channel builder named "Lounge" in event-guild
await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the channel on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two channels.
examples: await set {_channel} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Forum Post Builder
entities.description: A forum post that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: post tag
description: The tag applied to the post being built.
Only one tag can be set this way; multi-valued write-only properties are not supported yet.
examples: set post tag of {_b} to first element of available tags of {_forum}

syntaxes.name: auto archive duration
description: How long the post being built stays active without a message, in minutes.
Discord only accepts 60 (1 hour), 1440 (1 day), 4320 (3 days) or 10080 (1 week).
examples: set auto archive duration of {_b} to 10080

syntaxes.name: slowmode
description: The slowmode of the post being built, in seconds (0 disables it).

syntaxes.name: new forum post builder
patterns: [a] new [forum] post builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% with [the] [message] [content] %string% in [the] [channel] %forumchannel/mediachannel%
description: Creates a forum post builder. The post only exists once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new post builder named "I need help!" with message "please help me" in forum channel with id "000"
await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the post on Discord and returns its thread channel. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two posts.
examples: await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Invite Builder
entities.description: An invite that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: invite max uses
description: How many times the invite being built may be used before it expires (0 = unlimited).
examples: set invite max uses of {_b} to 1

syntaxes.name: invite max age
description: How long the invite being built stays valid, in seconds (0 = never expires).
examples: set invite max age of {_b} to 86400

syntaxes.name: invite temporary
description: Whether members joining through the invite being built are kicked once they disconnect, unless a role is assigned to them first.
examples: set invite temporary of {_b} to true

syntaxes.name: invite unique
description: Whether a brand new invite is created instead of reusing an existing similar one.
examples: set invite unique of {_b} to true

syntaxes.name: new invite builder
description: Creates an invite builder for a channel. The invite is only created on Discord once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new invite builder in event-channel
set invite max uses of {_b} to 10
set invite max age of {_b} to 3600
await set {_invite} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the invite on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two invites.
examples: await set {_invite} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Message Builder
entities.description: A message that has not been sent yet: configure it, then send it with 'the build result of'. Nothing reaches Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request, and the result is the sent message itself.

syntaxes.name: discord content
description: The raw text of the message being built. Setting it replaces whatever content the builder already carries.
examples: set discord content of {_m} to "hello world"

syntaxes.name: embed
description: The embed of the message being built. Setting it replaces every embed the builder already carries.

syntaxes.name: embeds
description: Every embed of the message being built, in display order (10 at most, Discord's limit).

Setting it replaces the embeds the builder already carries, adding appends to them and deleting removes them all. Each embed is snapshotted when it is set or added: editing it afterwards changes nothing. Embeds have no id, so removing a single one is not supported: set the list again.
The list cannot be read back from a builder; read 'embeds of' the sent message instead.
examples: set {_m} to a new message with content "Weekly report" in event-channel
await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}
send "%size of embeds of {_sent}%" to console

syntaxes.name: attached poll
description: The poll of the message being built (a message carries one poll at most; setting it replaces the previous one). The poll is validated and snapshotted when set.
A poll cannot be combined with components V2 (containers, sections, text displays...).

syntaxes.name: tts
description: Whether the message being built is read out loud by Discord's text-to-speech.

syntaxes.name: suppressed embeds
description: Whether Discord hides the embeds of the message being built, including the previews it generates from links.
examples: set suppressed embeds of {_m} to true

syntaxes.name: suppressed notifications
description: Whether the message being built is sent silently, without pinging anyone's device.
examples: set suppressed notifications of {_m} to true

syntaxes.name: referenced message
description: The message the one being built replies to.
examples: set referenced message of {_m} to event-message

syntaxes.name: mention replied user
description: Whether replying pings the author of the referenced message. Has no effect unless a referenced message is set.
examples: set mention replied user of {_m} to false

syntaxes.name: fail on invalid reply
description: Whether sending fails when the referenced message no longer exists. When false, the message is sent as a normal one instead.
examples: set fail on invalid reply of {_m} to false

syntaxes.name: attachments
description: The files attached to the message being built, read back as their names.
Add file uploads to it (see 'a new file upload'); remove one by its name.
examples: set {_f} to a new file upload from url "https://example.com/logo.png"

syntaxes.name: new message with content
description: Creates a message builder from a piece of text. The message is only sent once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_m} to a new message with content "hello" in event-channel
await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}

syntaxes.name: new message with embed
description: Creates a message builder from an embed. The message is only sent once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_e} to a new discord embed
set {_m} to a new message with embed {_e} in event-channel
await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Sends the message and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Sending the same builder twice sends two messages.
examples: await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}
await set {_sent} to the built message from {_m}

entities.name: Role Builder
entities.description: A role that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: hoisted
description: Whether the role being built is displayed separately in the member list.

syntaxes.name: mentionable
description: Whether the role being built can be mentioned by anyone.

syntaxes.name: new role builder
description: Creates a role builder. The role is only created on Discord once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new role builder named "Moderator" in event-guild
await set {_role} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the role on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two roles.
examples: await set {_role} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: color
description: The color of a Discord entity: a role's color, an embed's side bar, or the color a role builder will be created with. On a Skript that has the native Property.COLOR, "color of %x%" is the same expression that colors a block or a firework, dispatched per runtime type; on one that does not, it is "discord color of %x%".
Write-only on a role builder and on an embed builder: JDA exposes no getter on either, so reading them gives <none>.
examples: set color of event-role to orange

entities.name: Scheduled Event Builder
entities.description: A scheduled event that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: description
description: The description of the scheduled event being built.
examples: set description of {_b} to "Bring your own drinks"

syntaxes.name: start date
description: Overrides the start date the builder was created with.
examples: set start date of {_b} to (2 hours after now)

syntaxes.name: end date
description: The end date of the scheduled event being built. External events only.
examples: set end date of {_b} to (6 hours after now)

syntaxes.name: cover
description: The cover image of the scheduled event being built, as a URL or a local file path.

syntaxes.name: new channel event builder
patterns: [a] new scheduled[( |-)]event builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% in [the] [channel] %guildchannel% starting [at] %date%
description: Creates a builder for an event held in a channel. Discord ends it by itself, so no end date is given.
Only stage and voice channels can host a scheduled event.
examples: set {_b} to a new scheduled event builder named "Let's Talk Together" in stage channel with id "000" starting (5 hours after now)
await set {_event} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new external event builder
patterns: [a] new scheduled[( |-)]event builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% at %string% starting [at] %date% [and] ending [at] %date% in [the] [guild] %guild%
description: Creates a builder for an event happening outside of Discord. It needs both a start and an end date, since nothing tells Discord when it is over.
examples: set {_b} to a new scheduled event builder named "Concert" at "6 route of XXX" starting (1 hour after now) and ending (5 hours after now) in event-guild
set description of {_b} to "Come as you are"
await set {_event} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the scheduled event on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two events.
examples: await set {_event} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Thread Builder
entities.description: A thread that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: auto archive duration
description: How long the thread being built stays active without a message, in minutes.
Discord only accepts 60 (1 hour), 1440 (1 day), 4320 (3 days) or 10080 (1 week).
examples: set auto archive duration of {_b} to 4320

syntaxes.name: invitable
description: Whether non-moderators can add other members to the private thread being built.

syntaxes.name: slowmode
description: The slowmode of the thread being built, in seconds (0 disables it).

syntaxes.name: new private thread builder
patterns: [a] new private thread builder [(named|with [the] name)] %string% in [the] [channel] %threadcontainer%
description: Creates a private thread builder.
Private threads require the guild to be boost level 2 or higher; building one in a lower-level guild fails.
examples: set {_b} to a new private thread builder named "Staff Room" in event-channel
await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new thread builder
description: Creates a public thread builder. The thread only exists once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new thread builder named "Discussion" in event-channel
set auto archive duration of {_b} to 1440
await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new thread builder from message
description: Creates a public thread builder anchored to an existing message, in the channel that message was sent in.
examples: set {_b} to a new thread builder named "About this" from event-message
await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the thread on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two threads.
examples: await set {_thread} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Webhook Builder
entities.description: A webhook that does not exist yet: configure it, then create it with 'the build result of'. Nothing is sent to Discord until then, so setting its properties costs no request.

syntaxes.name: webhook avatar
description: The avatar of the webhook being built, as a URL or a local file path.

syntaxes.name: new webhook builder
description: Creates a webhook builder for a channel. The webhook only exists once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_b} to a new webhook builder named "Announcer" in event-channel
await set {_webhook} to the build result of {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Creates the webhook on Discord and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two webhooks.
examples: await set {_webhook} to the build result of {_b}

entities.name: Webhook Message Builder
entities.description: A message a webhook has not sent yet: configure it, then send it with 'the build result of'. Nothing reaches Discord until then, and the result is the sent message itself, which can later be edited or deleted through the same webhook.

syntaxes.name: webhook username
description: The name the webhook displays for this message only, instead of its own.

syntaxes.name: webhook avatar url
description: The image URL the webhook displays as its avatar for this message only.
examples: set webhook avatar url of {_m} to "https://example.com/avatar.png"

syntaxes.name: webhook thread
description: The thread the message is posted in. The webhook must belong to the thread's parent channel.

syntaxes.name: webhook thread id
description: The id of the thread the message is posted in, for when only the id is known.
examples: set webhook thread id of {_m} to "123456789012345678"

syntaxes.name: new webhook message with content
description: Creates a webhook message builder from a piece of text. The message is only sent once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_m} to a new webhook message with content "hello" through {_hook}
await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}

syntaxes.name: new webhook message with embed
description: Creates a webhook message builder from an embed. The message is only sent once you read 'the build result of' it, which requires 'await'.
examples: set {_m} to a new webhook message with embed {_embed} through {_hook}
await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Sends the message through the webhook and returns it. Requires 'await'.
Sending the same builder twice sends two messages.
examples: await set {_sent} to the build result of {_m}

syntaxes.name: bitrate
description: The audio bitrate (in bits per second) of this voice/stage channel.

syntaxes.name: user limit
description: The maximum number of members that can connect to this audio channel at once (0 = no limit).

syntaxes.name: region
description: The raw voice region of this audio channel, or null when it is automatic.

syntaxes.name: members
description: The members currently connected to this audio (voice/stage) channel.

syntaxes.name: audio channel with id
description: The voice or stage channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to audio channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: child channels
description: All guild channels that belong to this category.

syntaxes.name: category with id
description: The category with the given id, from cache.

syntaxes.name: channel with id
description: The channel of any kind with the given id, from cache.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

syntaxes.name: forum channel with id
description: The forum channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to forum channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: guild channel with id
description: The guild channel of any kind with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to guild channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: jump url
description: The jump-to URL of a message or a guild channel. Clicking it in the Discord client jumps straight to the message/channel. Co-owned across both types, so "jump url of %message/channel%" works on either.
examples: reply with jump url of event-message

syntaxes.name: guild
description: The guild a Discord entity belongs to: a member's, message's, role's, channel's, webhook's, sticker's, emoji's or scheduled event's guild. Co-owned across every such type, so "guild of %x%" works on any of them (null when the entity is not tied to a guild, e.g. a message from DMs).
examples: reply with name of guild of event-message

syntaxes.name: slowmode
description: The slowmode of the channel — the number of seconds a member must wait between messages.

syntaxes.name: pinned messages
description: The pinned messages of a channel. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Only the most recent page (up to 50 pins) is returned.
examples: await set {_pins::*} to pinned messages of event-channel

syntaxes.name: message channel with id
description: The channel messages can be sent in (text, news, voice, thread, private...) with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to message channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: send typing
description: Sends the typing status to a channel - what makes the "X is typing..." indicator appear.
It lasts 10 seconds, or until the bot posts a message.

syntaxes.name: news channel with id
description: The news channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to news channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: private channel user
description: The user this private (DM) channel is with, or null if it cannot be resolved.
examples: reply with private channel user of event-channel

syntaxes.name: stage instance
description: The active stage instance of this stage channel, or null when no stage is live.
examples: if stage instance of event-channel is set:

syntaxes.name: stage channel with id
description: The stage channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to stage channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: channel position
description: The position (ordering index) of this channel within its guild.

syntaxes.name: category
description: The parent category of this channel, or null if it is not inside a category.
examples: reply with name of category of event-channel

syntaxes.name: topic
description: The topic of this channel, or null if none is set.

syntaxes.name: nsfw
description: Whether this channel is marked as age-restricted (NSFW).
examples: if nsfw of event-channel is true:

syntaxes.name: channel webhooks
description: All webhooks of this channel. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
examples: await set {_webhooks::*} to channel webhooks of event-channel

syntaxes.name: text channel with id
description: The text channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to text channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: discord owner
description: The member who created this thread, or null if they are no longer in the guild.

syntaxes.name: message count
description: The number of messages currently tracked in this thread.

syntaxes.name: archived
description: Whether this thread is archived.
examples: if archived of event-channel is true:

syntaxes.name: locked
description: Whether this thread is locked.
examples: if locked of event-channel is true:

syntaxes.name: thread members
description: The members who joined this thread. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
The 'guild members' intent is required.
examples: await set {_members::*} to thread members of event-channel

syntaxes.name: start message
description: The message this thread started from. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
For a forum post, this is the post's first message.
examples: await set {_message} to start message of event-channel

syntaxes.name: public
description: Whether this thread is a public one (anyone who can see the parent channel can join it).

syntaxes.name: thread channel with id
description: The thread channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to thread channel with id "123"

syntaxes.name: archive thread
description: Archives a thread, closing it to new messages until someone posts again.

syntaxes.name: lock thread
description: Locks a thread: only moderators can unarchive it afterwards.

syntaxes.name: unarchive thread
description: Re-opens an archived thread.

syntaxes.name: unlock thread
description: Unlocks a locked thread.

syntaxes.name: threads
description: The thread channels currently held by this channel.

syntaxes.name: archived threads
description: The archived public thread channels of this channel. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
Only the most recent page is returned.
examples: await set {_threads::*} to archived threads of event-channel

syntaxes.name: archived private threads
description: The archived private thread channels of this channel. Fetched online, so it requires 'await'.
The bot needs the 'manage threads' permission, and only the most recent page is returned.
examples: await set {_threads::*} to archived private threads of event-channel

syntaxes.name: voice status
description: The custom voice status text currently set on this voice channel.

syntaxes.name: voice channel with id
description: The voice channel with the given id, from cache.
examples: set {_c} to voice channel with id "123"

entities.name: Application Command
entities.description: A slash, user or message command as Discord sees it: what 'update the discord commands' and 'register the discord command' push, and what 'registered commands of' brings back. Made by 'a new slash/user/message command', by the 'slash command' / 'user command' / 'message command' structures (read them back with 'structured slash command "name"'), or retrieved from Discord.

syntaxes.name: command id
description: The Discord id of the command, known once it was registered or retrieved; none before.
examples: send command id of {_cmd} to console

syntaxes.name: command type
description: "slash", "user" or "message".

syntaxes.name: enabled for
description: The permissions a member needs to see and use the command by default (admins always can). Empty means everyone.
Setting it to nothing re-enables the command for everyone; see 'disabled' to hide it from everyone.
examples: set enabled for of {_cmd} to manage server and ban members
add kick members to enabled for of {_cmd}

syntaxes.name: disabled
description: Whether the command is hidden from everyone but administrators by default.

syntaxes.name: nsfw
description: Whether the command is age-restricted (only usable in NSFW channels and by adult users).

syntaxes.name: contexts
description: Where the command can be used: guild, bot dm and/or group dm. Discord's default is guild only.
examples: set contexts of {_cmd} to guild and bot dm

syntaxes.name: integration types
description: How the command is installed: guild install (the default) and/or user install.
examples: set integration types of {_cmd} to guild install and user install

syntaxes.name: name localizations
description: The translated names, as "locale: text" lines. Set them with 'localize the name of ...'.

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Message Command
entities.description: A context-menu command shown when right-clicking a message (Apps > name). It has a name and nothing else; answer it in 'on message command' with 'target message', or declare it with the 'message command' structure.

syntaxes.name: new message command
description: Creates a message context-menu command. Its name may contain spaces and capitals (1 to 32 characters).
examples: set {_cmd} to a new message command named "Pin this"
register the discord command {_cmd} in event-guild

entities.name: Slash Choice
entities.description: One fixed choice of a slash option: the name the user sees and the value the script gets. Also what 'return choices' sends back from 'on slash completion'.

syntaxes.name: choice value
description: The value sent to the bot when this choice is picked (a text or a number).

syntaxes.name: new choice
description: Creates a choice. Give a text value for a string option, a number for an integer or number option.
examples: add a new choice named "Red" with value "red" to choices of {_opt}
return choices (a new choice named "One" with value 1)

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Slash Command
entities.description: A '/name' command with a description and, either, options or subcommands (grouped or not). Build one, fill it with the properties, then push it with 'update the discord commands' or 'register the discord command'. Use 'on slash command' to answer it, or declare it with the 'slash command' structure so its trigger runs on its own.

syntaxes.name: description localizations
description: The translated descriptions, as "locale: text" lines. Set them with 'localize the description of ...'.

syntaxes.name: options
description: The options (arguments) of a slash command or a subcommand, in order.
A command with subcommands cannot have options of its own.
examples: add a new user option named "target" with description "Who" to options of {_cmd}

syntaxes.name: subcommands
description: The subcommands ('/root sub') directly under a slash command or under a subcommand group.

syntaxes.name: subcommand groups
description: The subcommand groups ('/root group sub') of a slash command.

syntaxes.name: new slash command
patterns: [a] new slash command (named|with [the] name) %string% with [the] desc[ription] %string%
description: Creates a slash command. The name must be lowercase, 1 to 32 characters, without spaces.
examples: set {_cmd} to a new slash command named "ping" with description "Pong!"
add a new string option named "text" with description "What to echo" to options of {_cmd}
update the discord commands {_cmd} in event-guild

entities.name: Slash Option
entities.description: One argument of a slash command or subcommand: a Discord type, a name, a description, and optionally choices, autocomplete, bounds or channel types. Read its value in 'on slash command' with 'slash option "name"'.

syntaxes.name: option type
description: The Discord type of the option.
examples: if option type of {_opt} is string:

syntaxes.name: required
description: Whether the user has to fill this option. Required options must come before optional ones.

syntaxes.name: auto complete
description: Whether Discord asks the bot for suggestions while the user types ('on slash completion' + 'return choices'). Only string, integer and number options; incompatible with fixed choices.
examples: set auto complete of {_opt} to true

syntaxes.name: choices
