description: The fixed choices (up to 25) the user picks from. Only string, integer and number options; a choice's value must match the option type.
examples: add a new choice named "Red" with value "red" to choices of {_opt}

syntaxes.name: min value
description: The lowest value accepted by an integer or number option.

syntaxes.name: max value
description: The highest value accepted by an integer or number option.

syntaxes.name: min length
description: The shortest text accepted by a string option (0 to 6000).

syntaxes.name: max length
description: The longest text accepted by a string option (1 to 6000).

syntaxes.name: channel types
description: The kinds of channel a channel option accepts (text, voice, category, ...). Empty means any.
examples: set channel types of {_opt} to text and voice

syntaxes.name: new slash option
description: Creates an option of the given Discord type (string, integer, number, boolean, user, channel, role, mentionable, attachment). It is optional and without autocomplete until you say otherwise.
For an option typed by a Skript type (a member, a colour, an enum with its choices), see 'a new typed ... option'.
examples: set {_opt} to a new string option named "reason" with description "Why"

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Subcommand Group
entities.description: A '/root group sub' level: a named group of subcommands under a slash command. Add subcommands to it, then add it to 'subcommand groups of' the slash command.

syntaxes.name: new subcommand group
patterns: [a] new sub[ ]command group (named|with [the] name) %string% with [the] desc[ription] %string%
description: Creates a subcommand group. Same naming rules as a slash command.
examples: set {_color} to a new subcommand group named "color" with description "Colour settings"

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Subcommand
entities.description: A '/root sub' entry of a slash command, with its own description and options. Add it to 'subcommands of' a slash command or a subcommand group.

syntaxes.name: new subcommand
description: Creates a subcommand. Same naming rules as a slash command.
examples: set {_ban} to a new subcommand named "ban" with description "Ban someone"

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: User Command
entities.description: A context-menu command shown when right-clicking a user (Apps > name). It has a name and nothing else; answer it in 'on user command' with 'target user', or declare it with the 'user command' structure.

syntaxes.name: new user command
description: Creates a user context-menu command. Its name may contain spaces and capitals (1 to 32 characters).
examples: set {_cmd} to a new user command named "Report user"
register the discord command {_cmd} in event-guild

entities.name: File Upload Input
entities.description: A modal field where the user picks one or more files from their device. Read them in 'on modal received' with 'uploaded files of file upload with id'. It only lives inside a modal and needs a label there.

syntaxes.name: new file upload input
patterns: [a] new file upload input [with] [the] id %string% (named|labeled|with [the] label) %string%
description: Creates a file upload field for a modal (one file by default, see 'max range').
examples: set {_u} to a new file upload input with id "proof" labeled "Screenshot"

entities.name: Button
entities.description: A clickable button. A styled button carries an id you get back in 'on button click'; a link button opens a url instead and never fires an event; a premium button opens a sku purchase. A button needs a label or an emoji. Up to 5 buttons fit in one row.

syntaxes.name: label
description: The text shown on a button or a dropdown option, or the title above a text input or a dropdown inside a modal.
A text input or a dropdown added to a modal must have one.

syntaxes.name: custom id
description: The text id of a component: what 'clicked id' returns for a button, the key of a dropdown or a text input in the received values, the id of a modal.
A link or premium button has none.
examples: if custom id of event-button is "confirm":

syntaxes.name: url
description: The url a link button opens. Setting it turns the button into a link button.

syntaxes.name: emoji
description: The emoji shown on a button or a dropdown option. Accepts an emote, a unicode emoji or the '<:name:id>' form of a custom one.

syntaxes.name: disabled
description: Whether the component is greyed out and cannot be used.
examples: set disabled of event-button to true

syntaxes.name: new button
description: Creates a styled button (primary, secondary, success or danger) with the id you will read back as 'clicked id' when it is clicked.
The label and the emoji are optional here and can be set later, but one of them is required before the button is sent.
examples: set {_b} to a new primary button with id "confirm" named "Confirm"
set {_b} to a new danger button with id "delete" named "Delete" with emoji "🗑️"

syntaxes.name: new link button
patterns: [a] new link button [with] [the] url %string% [(named|with [the] label) %-string%] [with [the] emoji %-emote/string%]
description: Creates a button that opens a url when clicked. It never fires 'on button click'.
examples: set {_b} to a new link button with url "https://disky.me" named "Docs"

syntaxes.name: new premium button
description: Creates a button that opens the purchase flow of one of the application's skus. Discord draws its label itself.
examples: set {_b} to a new premium button with sku id "1234567890"

syntaxes.name: style
description: The style of a button (its color) or of a text input (short or paragraph). Co-owned with Skript's native Property.STYLE.

entities.name: Checkbox Group
entities.description: A modal field where the user ticks any number of options. Read the ticks in 'on modal received' with 'values of checkbox group with id'. Its options are dropdown options (the emoji is ignored). It only lives inside a modal.

syntaxes.name: new checkbox group
description: Creates a checkbox group for a modal. Add options to it before showing the modal.
examples: set {_c} to a new checkbox group with id "toppings" labeled "Toppings"
add a new option with value "cheese" named "Cheese" to options of {_c}

entities.name: Checkbox
entities.description: A single yes/no box of a modal. Read it in 'on modal received' with 'value of checkbox with id' (true or false). It only lives inside a modal; its label is the text next to the box.

syntaxes.name: checked
description: Whether the box is ticked when the modal opens.

syntaxes.name: new checkbox
description: Creates a checkbox for a modal, unticked by default.
examples: set {_c} to a new checkbox with id "agree" labeled "I agree to the rules"

entities.name: Component
entities.description: Any message or modal component under construction: a button, a dropdown, a text input, a row, a container, a section, a text display, a separator, a media gallery, a file display or a thumbnail. Configure it with its properties, then add it to a message builder, a row, a container or a modal. It is copied at that moment, so later changes to the component do not affect what was added.

syntaxes.name: unique id
description: The numeric identifier of a component inside a message, distinct from its text id.
Discord assigns one when the message is sent; set it yourself to address the component later with 'replace component with unique id'.

entities.name: Container
entities.description: A components V2 box with an optional accent color on its left edge, holding text displays, sections, separators, media galleries, file displays and rows of buttons or dropdowns. A message carrying a container is a components V2 message: it can have no content and no embed.

syntaxes.name: accent color
description: The color of the stripe on the left edge of the container, like an embed's color.
examples: set accent color of {_c} to red

syntaxes.name: spoiler
description: Whether the container, file display, thumbnail or media gallery is blurred until clicked.

syntaxes.name: new container
description: Creates a container, optionally filled with components.
examples: set accent color of {_c} to red
add a new text display "**Hello**" to components of {_c}
add a new separator to components of {_c}

entities.name: Entity Dropdown
entities.description: A select menu listing the guild's users, roles or channels. Selecting fires 'on entity dropdown click' with 'selected entities'. An entity dropdown takes a whole row on its own.

syntaxes.name: select targets
description: What the dropdown lists: users, roles, channels, or several of them.
examples: set select targets of {_d} to users and roles

syntaxes.name: channel types
description: When the dropdown lists channels, restricts them to these kinds.
examples: set channel types of {_d} to text and voice

syntaxes.name: new entity dropdown
description: Creates a dropdown listing users, roles and/or channels of the guild.
examples: set {_d} to a new entity dropdown with id "pick" targeting roles
set {_d} to a new entity dropdown with id "pick" targeting users and roles

entities.name: File Display
entities.description: A components V2 block showing an uploaded file, downloadable by the reader.

syntaxes.name: new file display
description: Creates a file display from a file upload (see 'a new file upload').
examples: set {_f} to a new file upload from file "plugins/report.txt"
add a new file display from file {_f} to components of {_container}

entities.name: Media Gallery
entities.description: A components V2 grid of up to 10 images or videos, each from a url or a file upload.

syntaxes.name: gallery items
description: The images and videos of the gallery, read back as their urls. Add a url or a file upload.

syntaxes.name: new media gallery
description: Creates a media gallery, optionally filled with urls and file uploads.
examples: set {_g} to a new media gallery with images "https://example.com/a.png" and {_upload}

entities.name: Modal
entities.description: A pop-up form shown to the user in answer to a button click, a dropdown click or a slash command, with 'show modal'. Its text inputs and dropdowns are read back in 'on modal received'. It holds up to 5 components; each text input or dropdown needs a label.

syntaxes.name: new modal
description: Creates a modal with the given id (what 'received id' returns) and title.
examples: set {_m} to a new modal with id "feedback" titled "Your feedback"
add a new paragraph text input with id "body" labeled "Message" to components of {_m}

syntaxes.name: title
description: The title of an embed. Co-owned with Skript's native Property.TITLE.

entities.name: Radio Group
entities.description: A modal field where the user picks exactly one of several options. Read the pick in 'on modal received' with 'value of radio group with id'. Its options are dropdown options (the emoji is ignored). It only lives inside a modal.

syntaxes.name: new radio group
description: Creates a radio group for a modal. Add options to it before showing the modal.
examples: set {_r} to a new radio group with id "size" labeled "Size"
add a new option with value "s" named "Small" to options of {_r}
add a new option with value "l" named "Large" to options of {_r}

entities.name: Component Row
entities.description: A horizontal line of components on a message: up to 5 buttons, or one dropdown. You rarely need one: adding a button or a dropdown straight to a message builder puts it in a row for you. Build a row yourself to control exactly which buttons share a line.

syntaxes.name: components
description: The components inside a row, a container, a section, a modal or a message builder.
Add a component to it; the component is copied at that moment. Remove one by its unique id.

On a message builder, a bare button joins the last row of buttons when it has room, a bare dropdown gets a row of its own, and any container, section, text display, separator, media gallery or file display switches the message to components V2 (no content, no embed).

syntaxes.name: new row
description: Creates a row, optionally filled with buttons or one dropdown.
examples: set {_row} to a new row with {_yes} and {_no}

entities.name: Section
entities.description: A components V2 block of one to three texts with an accessory (a button or a thumbnail) on its right. Its texts are text displays; 'a new section with texts ...' wraps plain texts for you.

syntaxes.name: accessory
description: The button or thumbnail shown on the right of a section.
examples: set accessory of {_s} to a new thumbnail from url "https://example.com/logo.png"

syntaxes.name: new section
description: Creates a section. It needs an accessory and at least one text before it is sent.
examples: set {_s} to a new section with accessory {_thumbnail} with texts "**Title**" and "Some text"

entities.name: Dropdown Option
entities.description: One choice of a string dropdown. Its value is what 'selected values' returns; its label is what the user sees (defaults to the value).

syntaxes.name: option value
description: The value sent back when this option is selected.

syntaxes.name: default option
description: Whether this option is selected when the dropdown is first shown.
examples: set default option of {_o} to true

syntaxes.name: new option
patterns: [a] new [drop[( |-)]down] option [with] [the] value %string% [(named|with [the] label) %-string%] [with [the] description %-string%] [with [the] emoji %-emote/string%]
description: Creates an option to add to the options of a string dropdown.
examples: set {_o} to a new option with value "red" named "Red" with emoji "🔴"

entities.name: Separator
entities.description: A components V2 gap between two components, with or without a visible line.

syntaxes.name: divider
description: Whether the separator draws a line, or only leaves an empty gap.

syntaxes.name: spacing
description: How much room the separator takes: small or large.

syntaxes.name: new separator
description: Creates a separator with a visible line and the given spacing (small by default).
examples: add a new separator to components of {_container}
add a new large separator to components of {_container}

entities.name: Dropdown
entities.description: A select menu whose choices are options you define. Selecting fires 'on dropdown click' with 'selected values'; in a modal, its values are read with 'value of dropdown with id'. A dropdown takes a whole row on its own.

syntaxes.name: options
description: The choices of a string dropdown, read back as their values.
Add dropdown options to it; remove one by its value.
examples: add a new option with value "red" named "Red" to options of {_d}

syntaxes.name: default values
description: What is selected when the dropdown is first shown: option values for a string dropdown, users, roles or channels for an entity dropdown.
examples: add event-member to default values of {_entities}

syntaxes.name: placeholder
description: The greyed text shown in a dropdown or a text input while nothing is selected or typed.
examples: set placeholder of {_d} to "Pick a color"

syntaxes.name: min range
description: The least the user must provide: options selected in a dropdown, characters typed in a text input.

syntaxes.name: max range
description: The most the user may provide: options selected in a dropdown, characters typed in a text input.

syntaxes.name: required
description: Whether the user must fill this component before submitting the modal it sits in. Ignored on a message.

syntaxes.name: new dropdown
description: Creates a dropdown with the given id. Add options to it before sending it.
examples: set {_d} to a new dropdown with id "color"
set placeholder of {_d} to "Pick a color"
add a new option with value "red" named "Red" to options of {_d}
add a new option with value "blue" named "Blue" to options of {_d}

entities.name: Text Display
entities.description: A components V2 block of markdown text. It goes in a container, a section, a modal, or straight on a message.

syntaxes.name: new text display
description: Creates a text display with the given markdown text.
examples: add a new text display "# Welcome" to components of {_container}

entities.name: Text Input
entities.description: A text field of a modal. Read what the user typed in 'on modal received' with 'value of text input with id'. It only lives inside a modal, never on a message, and needs a label there.

syntaxes.name: default value
description: The text pre-filled in the input when the modal opens.

syntaxes.name: new text input
description: Creates a text input for a modal. The style is 'short' (one line, the default) or 'paragraph' (a text area).
examples: set {_i} to a new short text input with id "name" labeled "Your name"
set {_i} to a new paragraph text input with id "body" labeled "Your message"

syntaxes.name: style
description: The style of a button (its color) or of a text input (short or paragraph). Co-owned with Skript's native Property.STYLE.

entities.name: Thumbnail
entities.description: A small image shown as the accessory of a section, from a url or a file upload.

syntaxes.name: new thumbnail
description: Creates a thumbnail from an image url or a file upload.
examples: set {_t} to a new thumbnail from url "https://example.com/logo.png"

entities.name: Emote Builder
entities.description: A custom emote that does not exist yet: a name, an image and optionally the roles allowed to use it. Create it with 'the build result of', under 'await'. Nothing is read or sent until then: the image is downloaded or read from disk when the emote is built.

syntaxes.name: allowed roles
description: The roles allowed to use the emote being built. Empty (the default) means everyone can use it.
The roles must belong to the builder's guild.
examples: add role with id "123456789012345678" to allowed roles of {_b}
remove event-role from allowed roles of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new emote builder
patterns: [a] new emote builder named %string% with [the] image %string/fileupload% in [the] [guild] %guild%
description: Creates an emote builder. The image is an http(s) URL, a local file path or a file upload; it must be a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WEBP of 256 KB at most (a GIF makes an animated emote).
The name is 2 to 32 letters, digits or underscores. The bot needs the Create Expressions permission.
examples: set {_b} to a new emote builder named "party_blob" with image "https://example.com/blob.png" in event-guild
await set {_emote} to the built emote from {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Validates the builder, loads its image and creates the emote on Discord. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two emotes.
examples: await set {_emote} to the built emote from {_b}

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Sticker Builder
entities.description: A guild sticker that does not exist yet: a name, a file, a description and at least one tag. Create it with 'the build result of', under 'await'. Nothing is read or sent until then: the file is downloaded or read from disk when the sticker is built.

syntaxes.name: description
description: The description of the sticker being built: empty (the default) or 2 to 100 characters.
examples: set description of {_b} to "A blob that parties"

syntaxes.name: sticker tags
description: The tags of the sticker being built: the words or emojis Discord suggests it for. At least one is required, 200 characters at most once joined, and a tag cannot contain a comma.
examples: add "tada" and "party" to sticker tags of {_b}

syntaxes.name: new sticker builder
patterns: [a] new sticker builder named %string% with [the] (image|file) %string/fileupload% in [the] [guild] %guild%
description: Creates a sticker builder. The file is an http(s) URL, a local file path or a file upload: a PNG, APNG, GIF or Lottie JSON of 512 KB at most, ideally 320x320 pixels (Lottie stickers are reserved to verified and partnered servers).
The name is 2 to 30 characters. Add at least one tag before building it. The bot needs the Create Expressions permission.
examples: set {_b} to a new sticker builder named "Party Blob" with image "https://example.com/blob.png" in event-guild
set description of {_b} to "A blob that parties"
await set {_sticker} to the built guildsticker from {_b}

syntaxes.name: result
description: Validates the builder, loads its file and creates the sticker on Discord. Requires 'await'.
Building the same builder twice creates two stickers.
examples: await set {_sticker} to the built guildsticker from {_b}

syntaxes.name: name
description: The name of a Discord entity: a user's or member's account name, a guild's name, a role/channel name, a bot's define-name. Registered on Skript's native Property.NAME, so the idiomatic "name of %x%" works without colliding. For a member's server nickname or display name, use "effective name".

entities.name: Poll Answer Draft
entities.description: An answer of a poll that has not been sent yet: a text and an optional emoji. Once the poll is sent, its answers are read back as regular 'pollanswer' objects.

syntaxes.name: draft answer text
description: The text of a poll answer that has not been sent yet (55 characters at most).
examples: set draft answer text of {_a} to "Burger"

syntaxes.name: draft answer emoji
description: The emoji of a poll answer that has not been sent yet, as written in a message.
examples: set draft answer emoji of {_a} to "🍔"

syntaxes.name: new answer
description: Creates a poll answer with an optional emoji, to add to the answers of a poll builder.
examples: set {_a} to a new poll answer with text "Pizza" with emoji "🍕"
add {_a} to poll answer drafts of {_poll}

entities.name: Poll Builder
entities.description: A poll that has not been sent yet: a question, 1 to 10 answers, a duration and whether voters may pick several answers. Send it with 'post' / 'reply with', or attach it to a message builder with 'attached poll of'. It is validated when attached, and the attached poll is a snapshot: editing the builder afterwards changes nothing.

syntaxes.name: poll duration
description: How long the poll stays open once sent: from 1 hour to 7 days (24 hours by default).
examples: set poll duration of {_poll} to 3 days

syntaxes.name: multi answer
description: Whether voters may select several answers.
examples: set multi answer of {_poll} to true

syntaxes.name: poll answer drafts
description: The answers of the poll being built, in order (10 at most).
Add plain texts or 'a new poll answer' objects (to give an answer an emoji); remove one by its text.
examples: add "Pizza" to poll answer drafts of {_poll}
add (a new poll answer with text "Burger" with emoji "🍔") to poll answer drafts of {_poll}
remove "Pizza" from poll answer drafts of {_poll}

syntaxes.name: new poll
description: Creates a poll builder from its question (300 characters at most). Without an explicit duration it lasts 24 hours. Add at least one answer before sending it.
examples: set {_poll} to a new poll titled "Favorite food?"
add "Pizza" and "Burger" to poll answer drafts of {_poll}
set poll duration of {_poll} to 2 hours

entities.name: Welcome Channel
entities.description: One entry of a welcome screen: a channel, the short text shown next to it and an optional emoji. Immutable: to change one, create a new one and replace it in the builder.

syntaxes.name: welcome channel
description: The channel a welcome screen entry points to. Empty when the bot cannot see it.

syntaxes.name: new welcome channel
patterns: [a] new welcome channel for [the] [channel] %guildchannel% (with|and) [the] description %string% [(with|and) [the] emoji %-emote/string%]
description: Creates a welcome screen entry. The description is at most 42 characters; the channel must be a text, voice, stage, news or forum channel (not a category or thread).
The emoji is an emote, a unicode emoji or the '<:name:id>' form of a custom one.
examples: set {_rules} to a new welcome channel for channel with id "123" with description "Read our rules" with emoji "📜"

entities.name: Welcome Screen Builder
entities.description: A pending edit of a guild's welcome screen. Only the fields you set are sent. Nothing reaches Discord until you use 'update the welcome screen using'. Welcome channels set on a builder replace the whole list on Discord.

syntaxes.name: welcome screen enabled
description: Whether the welcome screen is shown to new members of the guild.
examples: set welcome screen enabled of {_b} to true

syntaxes.name: welcome channels
description: The channels the welcome screen will list (at most 5). Setting replaces the list; 'add' and 'remove' edit what the builder holds so far, and 'delete' empties it.
A fresh builder starts empty, not from the current screen: to extend the current list, retrieve the screen and set its channels first.
examples: set welcome channels of {_b} to {_a} and {_b}

syntaxes.name: update welcome screen
description: Sends a welcome screen builder to Discord, applying every field that was set on it.
The effect waits for Discord to answer, so the next line sees the new screen.
examples: await set {_screen} to the welcome screen of event-guild

syntaxes.name: new welcome screen builder
description: Creates a builder for the welcome screen of a guild. Needs the Manage Server permission.
examples: set {_b} to a new welcome screen builder for event-guild
set welcome screen enabled of {_b} to true

entities.name: Welcome Screen
entities.description: The welcome screen of a community guild, as it was when it was retrieved. It is a snapshot: edit it with a welcome screen builder, then retrieve it again.

syntaxes.name: description
description: The description shown at the top of the welcome screen, if any.
examples: await set {_screen} to the welcome screen of event-guild

syntaxes.name: welcome channels
description: The channels listed on the welcome screen (Discord allows at most 5).

syntaxes.name: guild
description: The guild a Discord entity belongs to: a member's, message's, role's, channel's, webhook's, sticker's, emoji's or scheduled event's guild. Co-owned across every such type, so "guild of %x%" works on any of them (null when the entity is not tied to a guild, e.g. a message from DMs).
examples: reply with name of guild of event-message

core.name: destroy
description: Deletes a Discord entity: a message, a role, any channel, a custom emoji, a webhook, a scheduled event, a guild sticker or an automod rule.
To delete several messages at once, use the purge effect instead.

core.name: post
description: Posts a text, an embed, a component or a poll in a message channel.
The sent message is discarded; build a message and read 'the result of' it to keep it.

core.name: ban by id
description: Bans a user ID from a guild without retrieving the member first.
Works on users who already left the guild.
examples: ban user id "000000000000000000" from event-guild due to "ban evasion"

core.name: webhook delete
description: Deletes a message that was sent through a webhook, by its message or its id.
A webhook can only delete its own messages. Name the thread when the message lives in one.

core.name: webhook edit
patterns: edit [the] webhook message %string/message% of [the] [webhook] [client] %webhookclient% (with|to show) %string/embedbuilder/component/messageaction% [in [the] thread %-threadchannel%]
description: Edits a message that was sent through a webhook, by its message or its id.
A webhook can only edit its own messages. Name the thread when the message lives in one.
examples: edit webhook message {_sent} of {_hook} to show "Updated!"
edit the webhook message "123456789012345678" of {_hook} with {_embed}

core.name: Await
description: Runs an effect on a background thread and waits for it to fully complete before continuing.
On a DiSky REST property change this blocks until Discord confirms the change (instead of fire-and-forget); on a dual cache/online property read it uses the online value.
Redundant on effects that are already async.
examples: await set nickname of event-member to "DiSky"
await set {_members::*} to members of event-guild

core.name: New Discord Bot
description: A new, unconnected Discord bot to configure and then log in.
examples: set {_bot} to a new discord bot

core.name: Activity
description: Builds a Discord activity (what a bot is shown doing) to give to the activity of a bot.
A streaming activity needs a valid Twitch or YouTube url, otherwise Discord shows it as playing.
examples: set activity of {_bot} to watching "the server"
set activity of {_bot} to listening to "music"
set activity of {_bot} to streaming "live" with the url "https://twitch.tv/someone"
set activity of {_bot} to custom status of "Open for tickets"

core.name: Login Bot
description: Connects a configured bot to Discord under the given name. Validation/phase errors are reported cleanly.
examples: set {_bot} to a new discord bot

core.name: Shutdown Bot
description: Disconnects the given bot(s) from Discord and unloads them. The bot can be logged in again afterwards.

core.name: Recommended Shard Count
description: The value (-1) that tells DiSky to use Discord's recommended shard count.
examples: set shard count of {_bot} to recommended shard count

core.name: Define Bot
description: Declares and logs in a Discord bot from a config block — a reload-safe convenience over
'a new discord bot' + 'login'. The token is required; intents/cache/shard/activity/status are
optional. Lifecycle is handled by the global on ready / on shutdown events.

core.name: Try / Catch
description: Runs a block and catches any DiSky runtime errors. On error, jumps to the catch block with the
caught discorderror(s) stored in the given variable. Add 'and stop' to halt the trigger afterwards.
examples: reply with "Could not ban: %error meaning of {_errors::1}%"

core.name: Last Discord Error
description: The most recent Discord error that occurred (anywhere), as a discorderror. None if no error has occurred yet.
examples: if the last discord error is set:
reply with "Failed: %error meaning of the last discord error%"

core.name: Bots
description: All loaded bots, or the bot(s) with a given name (as defined by a `define bot` structure).
examples: set {_bot} to the bot named "my bot"

core.name: New Embed
description: A new, empty Discord embed to configure via the embed properties.
examples:
set {_embed} to a new discord embed
set title of {_embed} to "Hello"
set description of {_embed} to "World"
set color of {_embed} to red
loop 5 times:
    add (a new field named "Ping" with value "%random number between loop-value and loop-value + 100%ms" with inline true) to fields of {_embed}

core.name: New Embed Field
patterns: [a] new [embed] field (named|with name) %string% with [the] value %string% [[with] inline %-boolean%]
[a] new inline [embed] field (named|with name) %string% with [the] value %string%
description: A new embed field with a name and a value, optionally inline, to add to an embed.
examples: add (a new field named "Ping" with value "42ms") to fields of {_embed}
set {_field} to a new inline embed field named "Status" with value "OK"

core.name: Reply With
description: Replies to the current event: in a message event the reply is posted in the event's channel, in an interaction event (slash command, button, ...) it answers the interaction.
'hidden' makes an interaction reply ephemeral (only the user who triggered it sees it); it is ignored outside interactions.
'with reference' links the reply to a message, like Discord's own reply feature.
A message builder can be replied with too: its content, embeds, attachments and poll are sent, its own channel is ignored. A component (a container, a row, a button...) is sent on its own.
examples: reply with hidden "Only you can see this"

core.name: New File Upload
patterns: [a] new file upload from [local] file %string% [(named|with [the] name) %-string%] [with spoiler %-boolean%]
[a] new file upload from ur(l|i) %string% [(named|with [the] name) %-string%] [with spoiler %-boolean%]
[a] new file upload from attachment %attachment% [(named|with [the] name) %-string%] [with spoiler %-boolean%]
description: A file to send to Discord, from a local file path, a URL, or an attachment of a received message (an image too, when SkImage2 is installed).
The name defaults to the file's own; 'with spoiler' hides it behind a spoiler.
Nothing is read or downloaded until the message carrying it is sent.
examples: set {_f} to a new file upload from file "plugins/DiSky/logo.png"
set {_f} to a new file upload from url "https://example.com/image.png" named "custom.png"
set {_f} to a new file upload from attachment {_attachment} with spoiler true

core.name: Show Modal
description: Opens a modal for the user who triggered the current interaction: a button click, a dropdown click or a slash command. It is the interaction's answer, so nothing else may have replied or deferred it before, and a modal cannot answer another modal.
What the user submits comes back in 'on modal received'.
examples: set {_m} to a new modal with id "feedback" titled "Your feedback"
add a new paragraph text input with id "body" labeled "Message" to components of {_m}

core.name: Defer Interaction
description: Acknowledges the current interaction without answering it yet, which buys up to 15 minutes to reply instead of the 3 seconds Discord gives by default. A later 'reply with' goes through the deferred answer.
'hidden' makes the eventual reply ephemeral. 'and edit' (on a button or dropdown click) acknowledges without any 'thinking...' state, for when the script will only edit the message.
examples: edit interaction components with a new row

core.name: Edit Interaction Components
description: Replaces every component of the message whose button or dropdown was just clicked, as the answer to that interaction (or through it, if it was deferred 'and edit').
Bare buttons are grouped into rows like on a message builder. Pass nothing to strip the components.
examples: set disabled of event-button to true

core.name: Replace Component
description: Swaps one component of a sent message, found by its text id (a button, a dropdown) or its unique id (any component, including text displays and sections inside a container), for a new one. Every other component is kept as it is.
Inside a button or dropdown click on that same message, the edit is the interaction's answer.
examples: replace the component with id "confirm" of event-message with {_disabledButton}
replace the component with unique id 42 in {_msg} with a new text display "Updated!"

core.name: Modal Value
patterns: [the] [modal] value[plural:s] of [the] (component|input|text[( |-)]input|drop[( |-)]down|entity drop[( |-)]down|radio group|checkbox group|checkbox|file upload [input]|upload) [with [the] id] %string%

[the] [selected] entit(y|plural:ies) of [the] (component|input|text[( |-)]input|drop[( |-)]down|entity drop[( |-)]down|radio group|checkbox group|checkbox|file upload [input]|upload) [with [the] id] %string%

[the] (uploaded|received) (file|attachment)[plural:s] of [the] (component|input|text[( |-)]input|drop[( |-)]down|entity drop[( |-)]down|radio group|checkbox group|checkbox|file upload [input]|upload) [with [the] id] %string%
description: What the user submitted in a modal, by the id of the component.

A text input gives its text; a dropdown, a radio group or a checkbox group give the selected values; a checkbox gives true or false; an entity dropdown gives the picked users, roles or channels ('selected entities of'); a file upload input gives the uploaded attachments ('uploaded files of').
examples: reply with hidden "Thanks for: %value of text input with id "body"%"
broadcast "%values of checkbox group with id "topics"%"
if value of checkbox with id "agree" is true:
broadcast "%uploaded files of file upload with id "proof"%"

core.name: Discord Command
description: Declares a command triggered by a message: '<prefix><name> <arguments>'. Arguments are written like
Skript's own commands ('<user>', '<n: number = 1>', '[<text>]'); Discord entities are resolved from a
mention, an id or a name before the trigger runs, so 'arg-1' / '{_n}' hold real values.
Entries: prefixes, aliases, description, usage, category, roles, permissions, bots, executable in
(guild, dm, threads, voice, text), cooldown, cooldown scope (user, guild, channel), permission message,
cooldown message, usage message, trigger. Without 'prefixes' the bare name matches.

core.name: Discord Command Argument
description: An argument of the current 'discord command', by index ('arg-1', 'the 2nd argument'), by type
('user argument', 'text argument-2'), the last one, or all of them. Only inside the trigger of a
discord command; a named argument ('<who: user>') is also available as '{_who}'.
examples: discord command ban <member> [<reason: text = no reason>]:

core.name: All Discord Commands
description: Every 'discord command' currently loaded, from every script.

core.name: Slash Command Structure
description: Declares a slash command: its path (up to three words: command, group, subcommand), its arguments as '<name: type>' (wrapped in [ ] when optional), and a trigger that runs when it is used. Every argument is available as '{_name}' and as 'arg-1' / 'user argument' in the trigger.

Entries: description (a text, or a section of 'locale: text' lines with en-US), name (a section of translated names), enabled for (permissions), disabled, nsfw, contexts, integration types, cooldown + cooldown scope + on cooldown, arguments (per argument: a description, or a section with description, choices and 'on completion request'), trigger.

Declaring 'slash command mod ban' and 'slash command mod kick' gives one '/mod' command with two subcommands; a 'slash command mod:' without trigger describes the root. Nothing is sent to Discord: register the result from 'on ready' / 'on guild ready' with 'update the discord commands (all structured application commands) in ...'.
examples: slash command mod ban <target: member> [<reason: string>]:
update the discord commands (all structured application commands) in event-guild

core.name: Context Command Structure
description: Declares a user or message context-menu command (Apps > name when right-clicking a user or a message) and the trigger that runs when it is used: 'target user' / 'target message' give what was clicked.
Entries: name (a section of translated names), enabled for, disabled, nsfw, contexts, integration types, cooldown + cooldown scope + on cooldown, trigger. The name may contain spaces and capitals.
Nothing is sent to Discord: register it with 'update the discord commands (all structured application commands) in ...' from 'on ready' / 'on guild ready'.

core.name: Structured Discord Commands
description: The commands declared by 'slash command' / 'user command' / 'message command' structures, as command objects ready to be pushed: every 'slash command mod ...' structure is merged into one '/mod' command.
By name (the root word of a slash command, the full name of a context command), or all of them.
examples: update the discord commands (all structured application commands) in event-guild
send "%size of subcommands of {_mod}% subcommands" to console

core.name: Registered Discord Commands
description: The application commands currently registered on Discord: globally for a bot, or for one guild. They come back as regular command objects (with their 'command id'), so they can be edited and pushed again.
This asks Discord, so it needs 'await'.
examples: await set {_cmds::*} to registered commands of event-guild
send "%name of loop-value% (%command id of loop-value%)" to console

core.name: Poll Voters
description: The users who voted for one answer of a poll. The answer is a poll answer object or its number (answers are numbered from 1 in the order they were declared); the message is the one carrying the poll, not the poll itself. Every page of voters is fetched.
This asks Discord, so it needs 'await'.
examples: await set {_voters::*} to the voters of poll answer 1 of event-message
loop poll answers of (poll of event-message):
await set {_v::*} to the voters of poll answer loop-value of event-message

core.name: Message History
description: Fetches messages from the history of a channel. 'last X messages of a channel' returns the most recent ones, newest first. 'X messages before a message' returns the ones sent before it, closest (newest) first; 'X messages after a message' the ones sent after it, closest (oldest) first. The reference message itself is never included.
Any amount works: above 100, the history is fetched page by page (one request per 100 messages). Fewer messages come back when the channel does not have that many. The amount must be at least 1.
The bot needs the View Channel and Read Message History permissions. This asks Discord, so it needs 'await'.
examples: await set {_msgs::*} to the last 10 messages of event-channel
await purge (the last 50 messages in event-channel)
await set {_older::*} to the 20 messages before event-message
await set {_newer::*} to the 5 discord messages after {_pinned}

core.name: Discord Permissions in Channel
description: The effective permissions of a member or a role in one channel: its guild-wide permissions, with the channel's overrides applied (@everyone first, then the roles, then the member's own override). An administrator, and the guild owner, have every permission everywhere.
In a thread, the overrides of the parent channel apply.
Read-only; change the allowed or denied discord permissions of the channel instead.
examples: set {_perms::*} to discord permissions of event-member in event-channel
if discord permissions of event-member in event-channel contain send messages:

core.name: Channel Permission Override
description: The permissions a channel explicitly allows or denies to one member or role (its permission override). Empty when the channel has no override for it; anything neither allowed nor denied is inherited from the guild-wide permissions.

Add, remove and set change the override on Discord, creating it if needed. Adding to the allowed permissions also takes them out of the denied ones (a permission cannot be both), and the other way around. Removing only clears them from the list you name: removing from the allowed permissions does not deny them, it makes them inherited again. Reset (or delete) removes the whole override, allowed and denied together.
In a thread, the override is the parent channel's: changing it changes the parent channel.
The bot needs the 'manage permissions' permission in the channel (or 'manage roles' guild-wide), and can only allow or deny permissions it has itself. Under 'await' the change waits for Discord.
examples: await add send messages to allowed discord permissions of event-member in event-channel
await add view channel to denied discord permissions of {_role} in {_channel}
remove send messages from denied discord permissions of event-member in event-channel
set {_denied::*} to denied discord permissions of {_role} in event-channel
await reset allowed discord permissions of event-member in event-channel

core.name: Emoji
description: An emoji from its name, its unicode character or the id of a custom one (an emote). Several texts give several emojis.

Each text is resolved in this order: a custom emoji id or its '<:name:id>' / '<a:name:id>' form, a unicode emoji ('😂'), then a name. With a guild, a name first looks for a custom emoji of that guild (case-insensitive), then for a Discord shortcode ('joy' or ':joy:', skin tones as 'thumbsup_tone2'). Without a guild, the shortcode comes first, then the custom emojis every loaded bot can see.
It reads the cache. With 'await', an id or a name missing from the cache is also looked up on Discord: in the guild when one is given, else among the bot's application emojis.
A text that matches nothing is a readable error and is skipped. Name the guild when two guilds may hold a custom emoji with the same name.

core.name: Sticker Named
description: The sticker of a guild with the given name, compared case-insensitively. Returns nothing when the guild has no such sticker.
It reads the guild's sticker cache. With 'await', a name missing from the cache is looked up on Discord.
examples: set {_sticker} to sticker named "wave" in event-guild
await set {_sticker} to the sticker with name "wave" from event-guild

core.name: Member Of User
description: The member a user is in a guild: the same person, with the guild-side data (nickname, roles, join date...). Returns nothing when the user is not in that guild.

It reads the member cache, which depends on the bot's member cache policy. With 'await', a member missing from the cache is fetched from Discord, and a user who is not in the guild is a readable error.
examples: set {_member} to member of event-user in event-guild
await set {_member} to the member of {_user} in guild {_guild}

core.name: Update Discord Commands
description: Replaces every application command of a bot (globally) or of a guild with the given ones: what is not in the list is removed from Discord. This is the one call to make from 'on ready' / 'on guild ready'.
Global commands take up to an hour to show up for users; guild commands are immediate. Discord limits how often a guild's command list can be replaced (200 times a day).
Once done, 'command id of' each command is known.
examples: update the discord commands (all structured application commands) in event-guild
set {_ping} to a new slash command named "ping" with description "Pong!"
update the discord commands {_ping} globally in event-bot

core.name: Register Discord Command
description: Adds or replaces (by name) one or more application commands of a bot (globally) or of a guild, leaving the other registered commands alone. Use 'update the discord commands' to replace the whole list.
Once done, 'command id of' each command is known.
examples: register the discord command {_cmd} in event-guild
register the discord commands {_a} and {_b} globally in event-bot

core.name: Unregister Discord Commands
description: Removes application commands from a bot (globally) or from a guild: by command object, by name, by id, or all of them.
A command object whose id is known is deleted directly; otherwise the registered commands are looked up and every one with that name (and type, for a command object) is removed.
examples: unregister the discord command "ping" from event-guild
unregister the discord commands {_cmd} globally from event-bot
unregister all the discord commands from event-guild

core.name: Localize Command
description: Sets the name or the description shown to users of a given Discord locale, for an application command, a slash option, a subcommand, a subcommand group or a choice (choices only have a name).
Locales are Discord's codes ("fr", "de", "en-GB", "pt-BR", ...) or language names ("french").
examples: set {_cmd} to a new slash command named "ban" with description "Ban someone"
localize the name of {_cmd} in "fr" to "bannir"
localize the description of {_cmd} in "fr" to "Bannir quelqu'un"

core.name: Slash Option Value
description: The value the user gave to an option of the current slash command, by option name. Typed after what Discord sent (a text, an integer, a number, a boolean, a user, a channel, a role, a mentionable, an attachment), or after the option type you ask for; 'as member' turns a user into the guild member.
For a command declared by a 'slash command' structure, '{_name}' and 'arg-1' are simpler.
examples: ban slash option "target" as member with reason slash option "reason"

core.name: Return Slash Choices
description: Answers an autocomplete request with up to 25 suggestions and stops the trigger. Give choices, or plain texts / numbers (used as both the label and the value).
Only in 'on slash completion' and in an 'on completion request:' section of a slash command structure.

core.name: New Typed Slash Option
patterns: [a] new typed %*classinfo% [slash] option (named|with [the] name) %string% with [the] desc[ription] %string%
description: Creates a slash option from a Skript type instead of a Discord option type: a member, a colour, a text channel, a player, or any enum (its constants become the choices, or an autocomplete past 25). The same types work as '<name: type>' arguments of a 'slash command' structure.
Read the value back with 'slash option "name"' (as the Discord type) or, in a structure, as '{_name}'.
examples: set {_opt} to a new typed member option named "target" with description "Who"
set {_opt} to a new typed gamemode option named "mode" with description "Which mode"

events.name: Bot Join Event
description: Fired when the bot joins a new guild/server. This event is useful for setting up initial configurations when the bot enters a new server, such as adding default roles, sending welcome messages, or initializing server-specific settings.

events.name: Bot Leave Event
description: Fired when the bot leaves a guild/server. This event can be used for cleanup operations or logging when the bot is removed from a server, either by being kicked, the server being deleted, or the bot owner removing it manually.

events.name: Bot Ready Event
description: Fired when a bot is fully loaded and connected to Discord. This event is triggered once all guilds are ready and the bot's connection to Discord is completely established. This is the ideal event to use for initialization code that needs to run once when the bot starts up, such as scheduling tasks or initializing resources.
examples: broadcast "Bot %event-bot% is now online and ready!"

events.name: Bot Shutdown Event
description: Fired when a bot is shutting down or being stopped. This event is triggered when the bot's connection to Discord is closing, which can happen during server restarts, plugin reloads, or manual bot shutdowns. It provides an opportunity to perform cleanup operations or save data before the bot goes offline.

events.name: Guild Ready Event
description: Fired when a guild is fully loaded and all its data is accessible. This event occurs for each guild the bot is connected to when starting up. It's fired before the global Ready event and indicates that guild-specific data like members, channels, and roles have been loaded and are available for use.

events.name: Channel Create Event
description: Fired when a channel is created.

events.name: Channel Delete Event
description: Fired when a channel is deleted.

events.name: Channel Applied Tags Update Event
description: Fired when a forum channel's applied tags are changed.

events.name: Channel Archive Timestamp/Date Update Event
description: Fired when a thread channel's archive timestamp is changed.

events.name: Channel Archived Update Event
description: Fired when a thread channel's archived status is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% archived status changed from %past event-boolean% to %event-boolean%"

events.name: Channel Auto Archive Duration Update Event
description: Fired when a thread channel's auto archive duration is changed.

events.name: Channel Bitrate Update Event
description: Fired when a voice channel's bitrate is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% bitrate changed from %past event-number% to %event-number%"

events.name: Channel Default Layout Update Event
description: Fired when a forum channel's default layout is changed.

events.name: Channel Default Reaction Update Event
description: Fired when a forum channel's default reaction is changed.
examples: broadcast "Default reaction of %event-channel%: %old default reaction% -> %new default reaction%"

events.name: Channel Default Sort Order Update Event
description: Fired when a forum channel's default sort order is changed.
examples: on channel default sort order change:

events.name: Channel Default Thread Slowmode Update Event
description: Fired when a forum channel's default thread slowmode is changed.
examples: on channel default thread slowmode change:
broadcast "Channel %event-channel% default thread slowmode changed from %past event-number% to %event-number%"

events.name: Channel Flags Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's flags are changed.

events.name: Channel Invitable Update Event
description: Fired when a thread channel's invitable status is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% invitable status changed from %past event-boolean% to %event-boolean%"

events.name: Channel Locked Update Event
description: Fired when a thread channel's locked status is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% locked status changed from %past event-boolean% to %event-boolean%"

events.name: Channel Name Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's name is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% was renamed from %past event-string% to %event-string%"

events.name: Channel NSFW Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's NSFW status is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% NSFW status changed from %past event-boolean% to %event-boolean%"

events.name: Channel Parent Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's parent category is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% was moved from %past event-category% to %event-category%"

events.name: Channel Position Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's position is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% position changed from %past event-number% to %event-number%"

events.name: Channel Region Update Event
description: Fired when a voice channel's region is changed.

events.name: Channel Slowmode Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's slowmode setting is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% slowmode changed from %past event-number% to %event-number% seconds"

events.name: Channel Topic Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's topic is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% had its topic changed from '%past event-string%' to '%event-string%'"

events.name: Channel Type Update Event
description: Fired when a channel's type is changed.

events.name: Channel User Limit Update Event
description: Fired when a voice channel's user limit is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% user limit changed from %past event-number% to %event-number%"

events.name: Channel Voice Status Update Event
description: Fired when a voice channel's status (video or voice) is changed.
examples: broadcast "Channel %event-channel% voice status changed from %past event-string% to %event-string%"

events.name: Application Command Cooldown
description: Fired when a slash, user or message command declared by a structure is used while its 'cooldown' is still running. 'remaining cooldown' is the time left. It is also the event the 'on cooldown:' section of the structure runs in. Cancelling it lets the command run anyway. The interaction still has to be answered: reply to it here, or cancel the event and let the trigger answer.
examples: reply with hidden "Wait %remaining cooldown% before using /%used command% again."

events.name: Discord Command Failed
description: Fired when a 'discord command' was recognised but refused: wrong channel, missing role or permission, cooldown, wrong bot or invalid arguments. 'failure reason' tells which ("invalid arguments", "wrong channel", "missing role", "missing permission", "cooldown", "wrong bot"); 'remaining cooldown' is set for a cooldown. The configured 'permission message' / 'cooldown message' / 'usage message' of the command is sent before this event fires; use this event for anything more custom.
examples: reply with "Wait %remaining cooldown% before using %name of event-discordcommand% again."

events.name: Discord Command Used
description: Fired when a message matches a 'discord command' structure, before its checks (channel, roles, permissions, cooldown) and before its trigger runs. Cancel it to stop the command entirely. 'event-discordcommand' is the command, 'used prefix' / 'used alias' / 'used arguments' tell how it was typed.

events.name: Message Command
description: Fired when someone click on a message application command. Use `used command` to get the command name and `target message` for the targeted message. Don't forget to either reply to the interaction. Defer doesn't work here.
examples: reply with "You used %used message command% on %target message%"

events.name: Slash Command
description: Fired when a user execute a specific slash command. Use 'used command' to get the command name. Don't forget to either reply or defer the interaction, You can only defer using the wait pattern  e.g: 'defer the interaction and wait [silently]. You can get value of arguments using 'argument "name" as string' for example.

events.name: Slash Command Completion Event
description: Fired when Discord requests argument autocompletion for a slash command. Use 'event-string' to get the command name. Use the 'return' effect to provide completion choices to the user. You can access the focused argument with 'current argument' and other argument values with 'argument "name" as type'.
examples: return choice "Option 1" with value "option1", choice "Option 2" with value "option2"

events.name: User Command
description: Fired when someone click on a user application command. Use `used command` to get the command name and `target user` for the targeted user. Don't forget to either reply to the interaction. Defer doesn't work here.
examples: reply with "You used %used user command% on %target user%"

events.name: Button Click
description: Fired when any button sent by the bot is clicked. You can use the `clicked id` to get the clicked button id, and `event-button` is the clicked button itself.  !!! info "Modal can be shown in this interaction!"
examples: reply with hidden "You clicked the button with id '%clicked id%'!" # This will defer the interaction!

events.name: Modal Received
description: Fired when a modal has been sent to the bot from any user. Use 'received modal' to get the modal id. Don't forget to either reply or defer the interaction.  !!! warning "Modal can NOT be shown in this interaction!"
examples: reply with hidden "You submitted the modal with id '%received modal%'!"

events.name: Entity Dropdown Click Event
description: Fired when a user selects one or more entities in an entity dropdown menu. This event provides access to the selected entities (users, roles, channels, etc.). Don't forget to either reply to or defer the interaction to acknowledge it. You can show a modal in response to this interaction.

events.name: String Dropdown Click Event
description: Fired when a user selects one or more choices in a string dropdown menu. This event provides access to the selected string values and dropdown details. Don't forget to either reply to or defer the interaction to acknowledge it. You can show a modal in response to this interaction.

events.name: Emoji Add
description: Fired when a new emoji is added to a guild. Requires the `emoji` cache flag and the `guild expressions` intent.
examples: send "New emoji added in %event-guild%: %event-emote%" to console

events.name: Emoji Name Update
description: Fired when the name of an emoji is updated. Requires the `emoji` cache flag and the `guild expressions` intent.
examples: send "Emoji %event-emote% was renamed in %event-guild%: %past event-string% -> %event-string%" to console

events.name: Emoji Remove
description: Fired when an emoji is removed from a guild. Requires the `emoji` cache flag and the `guild expressions` intent.
examples: send "Emoji %event-emote% was removed from %event-guild%" to console

events.name: Emoji Roles Update
description: Fired when the roles of an emoji are updated. Requires the `emoji` cache flag and the `guild expressions` intent.
examples: send "Emoji %event-emote% roles updated in %event-guild%" to console

events.name: DiSky Error Event
description: Fired on the main thread for every DiSky error that no 'try' block caught: a failed Discord request, a missing permission, a refused builder, an effect used in the wrong event. An error raised inside a 'try' block goes to its 'catch' and never reaches this event. Cancel the event to keep DiSky from printing the error to the console; cancel it before any 'wait' or Discord effect, the console decision is taken as soon as the trigger pauses. 'event-bot' is set when the error comes from a trigger of a DiSky event, and is empty otherwise (a request queued without a trigger behind it does not know its bot), so a 'seen by' filter only matches the errors whose bot is known. An error raised by this event's own trigger is printed and does not fire the event again.
examples: if error code of event-discorderror is 50013:
post "Missing permission: %error message of event-discorderror%" to text channel with id "1234567890"

events.name: AutoMod Execution
description: Fired when an automated automod response has been triggered through an automod Rule.  Can be used to get the channel, user content, keyword that was found, the automod response and the id of the automod rule,  the user, the id of the message which triggered the rule, the guild it occurred in, and the id of the alert message sent to the alert channel (if configured).

events.name: Guild Log Entry Create Event
description: Fired when a new log entry is created in a guild. Can be used to monitor administrative actions within a guild.
examples: broadcast "New audit log entry created in %event-guild% for action type %event-entry's type%"

events.name: Guild Ban Event
description: Fired when a user is banned from a guild. A member doesn't exist here because the member is not in the guild anymore!  Can be used to get the banned user, the author and the guild.

events.name: Guild Join Event
description: Fired when the bot joins a guild. Use this to set up initial configurations or welcome messages.

events.name: Guild Unban Event
description: Fired when a user is unbanned from a guild. Can be used to get the unbanned user, the author and the guild.

events.name: Guild AFK Channel Event
description: Fired when the AFK channel of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new channel, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% changed AFK channel from %past afk channel% to %current afk channel%"

events.name: Guild AFK Timeout Event
description: Fired when the AFK timeout of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new timeout value, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% changed AFK timeout from %past afk timeout% to %current afk timeout%"

events.name: Guild Banner Event
description: Fired when the banner of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new banner URL, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% changed banner from %past banner% to %current banner%"

events.name: Guild Boost Count Update
description: Fired when the boost count of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new count, and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% boost count changed from %past boost count% to %current boost count%"

events.name: Guild Boost Tier Update
description: Fired when the boost tier of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new tier, and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% boost tier changed from %past boost tier% to %current boost tier%"

events.name: Guild Icon Event
description: Fired when the icon of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new icon URL, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% changed icon from %past icon% to %current icon%"

events.name: Guild Name Event
description: Fired when the name of a guild is changed. Can be used to get the old/new name, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild name changed from '%past guild name%' to '%current guild name%'"

events.name: Guild Owner Event
description: Fired when the owner of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new owner, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% owner changed from %past owner% to %current owner%"

events.name: Guild Splash Event
description: Fired when the splash image of a guild changes. Can be used to get the old/new splash URL, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "Guild %event-guild% splash changed from %past splash% to %current splash%"

events.name: Invite Create Event
description: Fired when an invite is created in a guild. Can be used to get the invite properties,  the channel, the author and the guild.
examples: broadcast "New invite created in %event-channel% with code %event-invite's code%"

events.name: Invite Delete Event
description: Fired when an invite is deleted from a guild. Can be used to get the channel and the guild.

events.name: Member Avatar Event
description: Fired when a member changes their server-specific avatar.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% changed their server avatar. New URL: %member avatar url%"

events.name: Member Boost Event
description: Fired when a member boosts a server, which is detected through a system message in the server.

events.name: Member Boost Time Update Event
description: Fired when a member's boost time is updated, which can happen when they start or stop boosting a server.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% boost time updated from %past member boost time% to %member boost time%"

events.name: Member Join Event
description: Fired when a member joins a guild.

events.name: Member Leave Event
description: Fired when a member is removed from a guild either by leaving or being punished. Use the ban/kick event instead to check the exact reason.

events.name: Member Nickname Event
description: Fired when a member changes their nickname in a guild.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% changed their nickname from '%past member nickname%' to '%member nickname%'"

events.name: Member Accept Screen Event
description: Fired when a member has agreed to membership screen requirements. This can be useful for adding roles since the member is not fully available until they've accepted the screen requirements.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% has completed the membership screening in %event-guild%"

events.name: Member Self Deafen Event
description: Fired when a member deafens or undeafens themselves in a voice channel.
examples: if member deafen state is true:

events.name: Member Self Mute Event
description: Fired when a member mutes or unmutes themselves in a voice channel.
examples: if member mute state is true:

events.name: Member Timeout Event
description: Fired when a member is timed out (temporarily restricted from interacting with the server).
examples: broadcast "%event-member% has been timed out until %member timeout end%."

events.name: Member Voice Join Event
description: Fired when a member joins a voice or stage channel. This event also fires when a member moves from one voice channel to another.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% joined voice channel %joined voice channel%"

events.name: Member Voice Leave Event
description: Fired when a member leaves a voice or stage channel. This includes both disconnecting completely and moving to another channel.
examples: broadcast "%event-member% left voice channel %left voice channel%"

events.name: Role Add Event
description: Fired when a member receives new roles. This is a log action, so event-author returns who made the action and event-roles returns a list of added roles.

events.name: Role Remove Event
description: Fired when roles are removed from a member. This is a log action, so event-author returns who made the action and event-roles returns a list of removed roles.

events.name: Message Delete
description: Fired when any message is deleted. This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.

events.name: Message Edit
description: Fired when any message is edited / updated. This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.

events.name: Message Receive
description: Fired when a bot receives a message — in a guild or in private messages by default. Use 'event is from guild' to filter.

events.name: Poll Vote Add
description: Fired when a user adds their vote to a poll in a message.

events.name: Poll Vote Remove
description: Fired when a user removes their vote from a poll in a message.
examples: send "User %event-user% removed their vote from a poll in %event-channel%!" to console

events.name: Reaction Add
description: Fired when a message, that can be seen by the bot, receive a reaction. This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.

events.name: Reaction Remove
description: Fired when an user remove a reaction from a specific message. This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.

events.name: Reaction Remove All
description: Fired when an user remove every reactions from a message. This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.

events.name: Role Color Update Event
description: Fired when the color of a role changes. This event provides access to both the old and new colors of the role. It can be used for tracking aesthetic changes to roles or for synchronization systems.
examples: broadcast "Role %event-role% color changed from %past event-color% to %event-color%"

events.name: Role Create Event
description: Fired when a new role is created in a guild. This event provides access to the newly created role and the guild it belongs to. It's useful for tracking administrative changes or implementing role management systems.

events.name: Role Delete Event
description: Fired when a role is deleted from a guild. This event provides access to the deleted role and the guild it belonged to. It can be used for auditing purposes or to trigger cleanup actions in your bot.

events.name: Role Hoisted Update Event
description: Fired when the hoisted status of a role changes. Hoisted roles are displayed separately in the member list. This event provides access to both the old and new hoisted states. It's useful for tracking changes to role visibility in the member sidebar.
examples: broadcast "Role %event-role% is now shown separately in the member list"
broadcast "Role %event-role% is no longer shown separately in the member list"

events.name: Role Icon Update Event
description: Fired when the icon of a role changes. This event provides access to both the old and new icon URLs. It can be used for tracking visual changes to roles or updating external systems.
examples: broadcast "Role %event-role% icon changed from %past event-string% to %event-string%"

events.name: Role Mentionable Update Event
description: Fired when the mentionable status of a role changes. This event tracks whether a role can be mentioned by regular users. It provides access to both the old and new mentionable states. It's useful for tracking changes that affect role notifications and visibility.
examples: broadcast "Role %event-role% can now be mentioned by everyone"
broadcast "Role %event-role% can no longer be mentioned by everyone"

events.name: Role Name Update Event
description: Fired when the name of a role changes. This event provides access to both the old and new names of the role. It's useful for tracking role identity changes or updating external systems that reference roles by name.
examples: broadcast "Role name changed from '%past event-string%' to '%event-string%' in %event-guild%"

events.name: Role Permissions Update Event
description: Fired when the permissions of a role change. This event provides access to both the old and new permission sets. It's crucial for security monitoring, permission auditing, and tracking administrative changes.
examples: broadcast "Permissions for role %event-role% have been updated in %event-guild%"

events.name: Role Position Update Event
description: Fired when the position of a role changes in the role hierarchy. This event provides access to both the old and new positions. It's useful for tracking changes to the role hierarchy that may affect permissions.
examples: broadcast "Role %event-role% position changed from %past event-number% to %event-number%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Cover Image Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's cover image is changed. The old/new values are image URLs (or absent if no image is set). Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: on scheduled event cover image change:
broadcast "Cover image of %event-scheduledevent's name% changed to %new scheduled event cover image%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Create
description: Fired when a scheduled event is created in a guild. Can be used to get the scheduled event and the guild it was created in. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "A new scheduled event '%event-scheduledevent's name%' was created in %event-guild%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Delete
description: Fired when a scheduled event is deleted from a guild. Can be used to get the scheduled event and the guild it was deleted from. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "Scheduled event '%event-scheduledevent's name%' was deleted from %event-guild%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Description Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's description is changed. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.

events.name: Scheduled Event End Time Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's end time is changed. The old or new value may be absent if the event has no defined end time. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: on scheduled event end time change:
broadcast "%event-scheduledevent's name% will now end at %new scheduled event end time%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Location Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's location is changed. For external events this is a free-form string; for channel-bound events it is the channel ID as a string. Use 'event-channel' to access the new channel if the event is bound to a channel. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "%event-scheduledevent's name% moved from '%past scheduled event location%' to '%new scheduled event location%'"

events.name: Scheduled Event Name Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's name is changed. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "Scheduled event renamed from '%past scheduled event name%' to '%new scheduled event name%'"

events.name: Scheduled Event Start Time Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's start time is changed. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: on scheduled event start time change:
broadcast "%event-scheduledevent's name% will now start at %new scheduled event start time%"

events.name: Scheduled Event Status Update
description: Fired when a scheduled event's status changes between: scheduled, active, completed, cancelled. This is how you detect when an event actually starts (status becomes 'active') or ends (status becomes 'completed'). Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: if new scheduled event status is "active":

events.name: Scheduled Event User Add
description: Fired when a user subscribes (RSVPs as 'interested') to a scheduled event. The user/member may not be present if not cached. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "%event-user% is now interested in %event-scheduledevent's name%"

events.name: Scheduled Event User Remove
description: Fired when a user unsubscribes from a scheduled event. The user/member may not be present if not cached. Requires the SCHEDULED_EVENTS intent and the SCHEDULED_EVENTS cache flag to be enabled.
examples: broadcast "%event-user% is no longer interested in %event-scheduledevent's name%"

events.name: Guild Sticker Add
description: Fired when someone or something adds a sticker to a guild.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.
examples: send "New sticker added in %event-guild%: %event-sticker%" to console

events.name: Guild Sticker Available State Update
description: Fired when the Available State of a sticker is updated.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.
examples: on guild sticker available state update:

events.name: Guild Sticker Description Update
description: Fired when the Description of a sticker is updated.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.

events.name: Guild Sticker Name Update
description: Fired when the Name of a sticker is updated.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.

events.name: Guild Sticker Remove
description: Fired when someone or something removes a sticker from a guild.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.

events.name: Guild Sticker Tags Update
description: Fired when the tags of a sticker is updated.  For this event to work, the `sticker` cache flag and `guild expressions` intent are required.

events.name: Thread Join Event
description: Fired when a member joins a tread, either by joining itself or by a moderator  can be used to get the thread, the guild and the member.

events.name: Thread Leave Event
description: Fired when a member leaves a thread, either by leaving itself or by a moderator  can be used to get the thread, the guild and the member.

events.name: User Activity End Event
description: Fired when a user stops an activity in a guild. Activities include playing games, listening to music, streaming, or custom status messages. This event requires the 'guild presences' intent and the 'activity' cache flag to be enabled.
